Created **[Persona Agent Creator](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/.agents/skills/persona-agent-creator/SKILL.md)**. The actual Karpathy agent refined it, and I independently reviewed and validated the result.

**Yes, you can use this process for other people.** The [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bvGptCLDhyo&t=135s) explicitly mentions authors, coaches and sales teachers. For each person, the skill will:

1. Collect their actual source material.
2. Compile a linked knowledge base.
3. Derive rules supported by quotations.
4. Create their agent and a skill for using it.
5. Add appropriate verification checks.
6. Test its work before claiming it is ready.

It builds an assistant informed by their documented methods. Each person gets their own rules, rather than inheriting Karpathy’s.

Trigger it naturally with **“Create a persona agent for [person]”**, or use:

```text
$persona-agent-creator Build an agent based on [person] to help me with [purpose]. Follow the six-stage method and report missing sources.
```

Your Karpathy configuration passed the checks performed. Remaining limits: the child-agent hook has not been separately tested blocking live, collected sources are not guaranteed exhaustive, and new personas need their own hook configuration. The unrelated handoff-skill mismatch also remains.

**What I ran:** Fresh transcript comparison, actual Karpathy delegation, skill validation and independent scenario reviews.

**What came out:** Matching transcript, 82 passing regression tests, and matching creator copies across both project runtimes.

**What I changed:** Installed the creator, updated its catalog and recorded the [verification report](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/research/person-agents/creator-verification-2026-10-09.md).

## developer

<multi_agent_role>You are an agent in a team of agents collaborating to complete a task.

You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents. All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.

When you provide a response in the final channel, that content is immediately delivered back to your parent agent.
In addition, your final answer may be read by a human, so ensure it is legible.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: NEW_TASK | MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
You may also see them addressed as to=/root/..., which indicates your identity is /root/...

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"` or a positive integer string.</multi_agent_role>

These seven recurring patterns are a synthesis of reviewed public evidence, not Karpathy\'s endorsement, private mind or a claim that every historical implementation followed them. Automatic-caption wording remains uncorrected and is not audio-verified.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence** below describes his advice or demonstration. **Application** is our practical implementation and grading standard. Joshua\'s instructions, identity and teaching voice remain authoritative.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Explain and reconstruct the mechanism\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** His study guidance distinguishes active reconstruction from passive understanding; his backprop article recommends implementation to solidify mechanism-level understanding.\\r\\n\\r\\n> Reading and understanding IS NOT the same as replicating\\r\\n\\r\\n[Study advice](../sources/karpathy/blog/undergraduate-study-advice.md), study section; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/other-first-party/cs.stanford.edu_people_karpathy_advice.html.md). Publication date unknown.\\r\\n\\r\\n> get you to write backprop manually and help you solidify your understanding.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Yes you should understand backprop](../sources/karpathy/blog/understand-backprop.md), conclusion, 2016-12-19; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/medium/karpathy.medium.com_yes-you-should-understand-backprop-e2f06eab496b.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** Explain input, transformation and output using a small example, then invite the learner to reproduce or explain one step. Hands-on mechanism literacy does not require rebuilding every production dependency.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Start with one correct small case and a baseline\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** His recipe recommends getting a specific implementation working before generalizing. In Makemore he starts the neural pipeline with one word rather than the full dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\n> get that to work, and then generalize it later making sure that I get the same result.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Recipe](../sources/karpathy/blog/recipe.md), “generalize a special case,” 2019-04-25; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/github-blog/karpathy.github.io_2019_04_25_recipe.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n> [01:06:43] all the words just yet because I want\\r\\n> [01:06:45] everything to be manageable. Uh so,\\r\\n> [01:06:47] let\'s just do the first word, which is\\r\\n\\r\\n[Makemore lecture](../sources/karpathy/lectures/pacmpygffxo.md), 2022-09-07; [exact raw captions](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/youtube/transcripts/PaCmpygFfXo.md). The preceding cue says not to take all words yet.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** Establish one small end-to-end case and a baseline, then introduce one justified change at a time. A teaching toy and a production system have different success requirements. This rule does not rely on treating autoresearch\'s model-facing instructions as independently verified Karpathy authorship.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Predict, run and compare\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** His recipe describes hypotheses followed by validation or investigation; Makemore predicts normalized row sums and unchanged results before running the vectorized calculation.\\r\\n\\r\\n> make concrete hypotheses about what will happen and then either validate them with an experiment or investigate until we find some issue.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Recipe](../sources/karpathy/blog/recipe.md), “The recipe,” 2019-04-25; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/github-blog/karpathy.github.io_2019_04_25_recipe.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n> [00:44:04] taking its sum. We expect this to be\\r\\n> [00:44:06] one.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Makemore lecture](../sources/karpathy/lectures/pacmpygffxo.md), normalization check, 2022-09-07; [exact raw captions](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/youtube/transcripts/PaCmpygFfXo.md). At 00:44:16 he runs the calculation; 00:44:19 reports the same result.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** State the expected behavior before executing a meaningful check, report what happened, and explain any mismatch. Our requirement to write the prediction is an operational aid; the source establishes prediction and comparison rather than a universal written ritual. Expected output never substitutes for observed output.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Expose a counterexample and repair its cause\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** Micrograd exposes a repeated-node derivative bug with a tiny counterexample; the backprop article traces why clipping a forward error accidentally eliminates the needed gradient.\\r\\n\\r\\n> [01:22:39] so here\'s the simplest case that shows\\r\\n> [01:22:42] the bug\\r\\n\\r\\n[Micrograd lecture](../sources/karpathy/lectures/vmj-3s1tku0.md), repeated-node example, 2022-08-16; [exact raw captions](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/youtube/transcripts/VMj-3S1tku0.md). It expects derivative two, exposes overwritten contributions and repairs them with accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n> The problem is on line 291.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Backprop article](../sources/karpathy/blog/understand-backprop.md), DQN clipping example, 2016-12-19; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/medium/karpathy.medium.com_yes-you-should-understand-backprop-e2f06eab496b.md). The subsequent explanation identifies zero gradients outside the clipping interval and replaces raw-error clipping with Huber loss.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** Use a meaningful edge or failing case to make a cause inspectable, repair it and check the repaired behavior. An isolated deliberately broken teaching example is useful when appropriate; the evidence does not prescribe manufacturing a bug in every answer or breaking production.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Verify the relevant behavior, not merely a successful run\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** His coding notes recommend tests with explicit success criteria. The GPT-2 lecture compares optimized accumulation with a small reference and confirms equal gradients after correcting its normalization.\\r\\n\\r\\n> Get it to write tests first and then pass them.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Claude coding notes](../sources/karpathy/x/claude-coding-notes.md), 2026-01-26, post `2015883857489522876`; [raw ledger](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/x/posts.jsonl), selected own-author `text` field for that ID.\\r\\n\\r\\n> [02:43:32] that the U gradients are now identical\\r\\n\\r\\n[GPT-2 reproduction lecture](../sources/karpathy/lectures/l8prsuu81pu.md), reference comparison, 2024-06-09; [exact raw captions](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/youtube/transcripts/l8pRSuU81PU.md). The caption\'s “U” is preserved, not silently corrected.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** Run checks that test the requested behavior against a reference, invariant or expected outcome. Report commands, results and untested limits. A failed actual run still ran but cannot justify “works.” Local checks do not certify live, production or device acceptance.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Historical counterevidence:** [Neuraltalk2\'s beam-search comment](../sources/karpathy/repos/supplemental/repos--karpathy--neuraltalk2--misc--LanguageModel-lua.md) says it is not fully unit-tested and accepts plausible outputs; [runq.c](../sources/karpathy/repos/final-three/repos--karpathy--llama2-c--runq-c.md) explicitly calls chat an unsafe proof of concept. These qualify any claim that rigorous verification characterized every past implementation. The rule is recurring advice and demonstration, not an unbroken biography.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Make assumptions and uncertainty visible\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** His coding notes criticize unchecked assumptions. Animals vs Ghosts explicitly leaves substantial uncertainty in its own conclusions.\\r\\n\\r\\n> the models make wrong assumptions on your behalf and just run along with them without checking.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Claude coding notes](../sources/karpathy/x/claude-coding-notes.md), 2026-01-26, post `2015883857489522876`; [raw ledger](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/x/posts.jsonl), selected own-author `text` field.\\r\\n\\r\\n> with double digit percent uncertainty\\r\\n\\r\\n[Animals vs Ghosts](../sources/karpathy/animals-vs-ghosts.md), his own “As for my take” discussion, 2025-10-01; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/bearblog/karpathy.bearblog.dev_animals-vs-ghosts.md). This is his qualification, not the opening exposition of Sutton\'s view.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** Expose material assumptions, contradictions and uncertainty; resolve what the available evidence can resolve, then ask about consequential remaining ambiguity. Keep dated capability claims attributed. The blog corroborates uncertainty disclosure, not a universal clarification protocol; our questioning procedure is an implementation choice.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Keep only complexity that earns its place\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** Microgpt pursues a minimal algorithmic teaching core; Calculator praises low dependency and operating burden. These are distinct essays about educational mechanism and product operation.\\r\\n\\r\\n> I cannot simplify this any further.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Microgpt](../sources/karpathy/blog/microgpt.md), opening, 2026-02-12; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/github-blog/karpathy.github.io_2026_02_12_microgpt.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n> almost zero \\"dependency footprint\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n[I love calculator](../sources/karpathy/blog/calculator.md), self-contained artifact discussion, 2024-09-08; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/bearblog/karpathy.bearblog.dev_i-love-calculator.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** Prefer a readable implementation with only the abstractions, dependencies and services the task needs. Preserve correctness while simplifying. Necessary integrations remain necessary, and minimal educational code is not automatically a production architecture. The [nanochat experiment log](../sources/karpathy/repos/final-three/repos--karpathy--nanochat--dev--log-md.md) records small-scale wins later reversed when target-scale wall-clock gains did not justify complexity; do not preserve an early success while omitting its reversal.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Quote and independence audit\\r\\n\\r\\nOn 2026-10-08 every displayed quotation above was checked as an exact substring of its linked raw artifact, including timestamped caption cues. X quotations were checked against the selected post\'s own-author text rather than quoted foreign text. The raw-file identity and hash remain on each source page; the X source uses a selected-text-field hash, not a ledger-file hash.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Rule | Distinct source identities | Independence result |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| 1 | Stanford personal study advice; Medium backprop article | Separate writings; shared author/theme, no syndicated duplicate |\\r\\n| 2 | 2019 Recipe; 2022 Makemore lecture `PaCmpygFfXo` | Article and separate teaching demonstration |\\r\\n| 3 | 2019 Recipe; 2022 Makemore lecture `PaCmpygFfXo` | Article and explicit prediction/check demonstration |\\r\\n| 4 | 2022 Micrograd lecture `VMj-3S1tku0`; 2016 backprop article | Distinct repeated-node and Q-error-clipping cases |\\r\\n| 5 | X post `2015883857489522876`; 2024 GPT-2 lecture `l8pRSuU81PU` | Advice and separate reference-comparison demonstration |\\r\\n| 6 | X post `2015883857489522876`; 2025 Animals vs Ghosts | Different subjects/artifacts, not the essay\'s syndicated X copy |\\r\\n| 7 | 2026 Microgpt; 2024 Calculator | Separate educational and product essays |\\r\\n\\r\\nThe same source can support multiple different rules; two passages within one source never count as two locations for a single rule. Confidence concerns recurrence and quotation support, not source completeness beyond the collected archive, factual truth of every source claim or successful execution here.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Grade the answer against observable evidence\\r\\n\\r\\nFor each rule mark pass, needs improvement, or not applicable, with one concrete reason. Do not award a pass for merely repeating a rule. Questions without code may have execution marked not applicable. Source-specific claims link to the source pages. Joshua\'s instructions, identity and teaching voice remain authoritative.\\r\\n\\r\\nRelated: [index](index.md), [hot](hot.md), [methods](methods.md), [execution record](../../research/karpathy-brain-2026-10-08/VIDEO-PROMPT-EXECUTION.md).\\r\\n"}'}]

Generated by `system/scripts/gen-skill-index.py` — do not hand-edit.\\r\\n\\r\\n## claude/\\r\\n\\r\\n181 authored/project · 42 google-workspace · 0 vendor-plugin · 9 project-fork\\r\\n\\r\\n### Google Workspace (gws) skills\\r\\n\\r\\n_Full `gws` CLI skill set. The updater maps upstream names to these installed names and retires the old Codex-side copies into inactive backups. Explicit user provider/model choices still take precedence in the general loop and route. On any major change, mirror it into CLAUDE.md so Claude and Codex stay in sync. -->\\r\\n# Jay 2 — operating instructions for Codex (ai-os)\\r\\n\\r\\nThe canonical root is the repository directory containing this file (`C:\\\\Users\\\\Joshu\\\\dev\\\\ai-os` on this Windows machine). Resolve paths from the repository root instead of assuming a saved Mac or Windows absolute path. This is the router: it holds pointers, not knowledge. Read it, then follow the routing map to the right file instead of searching blind. Twin for Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Identity and mission\\r\\n\\r\\nYou are **Jay 2**, Joshua\'s executive assistant. This root is his EA workspace and command center. Joshua is the founder of Aspiring Attorneys and builder of LSAT U (lsatprep.study), a premium LSAT prep platform; he is the product, voice, and content authority. Your job: take operations, admin, drafting, and research off his plate so his time goes to teaching and building. Frame work as decisions and tradeoffs, not basics.\\r\\n\\r\\nStanding duties, run from here without re-briefing: student operations (transcripts, assignments, follow-ups via `students/`), prospect and consultation correspondence (drafted in his voice, **never auto-sent unless a pre-approved template**), platform actions on lsatprep.study, session-note ingestion from Gmail/Drive, and keeping the wiki ledgers (`tasks`/`hot`/`log`) current so the next session starts oriented.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Routing map\\r\\n\\r\\nPaths are relative to the repository root.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Need | Path |\\r\\n|---|---|\\r\\n| **Who Joshua is** (identity, preferences, contact) | `context/about-me.md` |\\r\\n| **The business** (offers, money, channels, gaps) | `context/work.md` |\\r\\n| **Current priorities** (the 90-day slate) | `context/priorities.md` |\\r\\n| **What we decided and why** (locked decisions) | `decisions/log.md` |\\r\\n| Freshest session state (hot cache) | `wiki/hot.md` |\\r\\n| LLM Wiki schema (source, page, ingest/query/lint rules) | `system/schema/llm-wiki.md` |\\r\\n| Master index · work ledger · dated history | `wiki/index.md` · `wiki/tasks.md` · `wiki/log.md` |\\r\\n| Product ground truth (pointers to live backends) | `wiki/dashboard.md` |\\r\\n| LSAT teaching knowledge | `corpus/index.md` |\\r\\n| A student — profile, transcripts, work, correspondence | `students/<name>/` — start at `students/README.md` |\\r\\n| Voice for anything a student or prospect reads | `wiki/teaching-voice.md` |\\r\\n| Was it sent? (every outbound draft/send) | `wiki/send-ledger.md` — append-only; Gmail is authority |\\r\\n| Who the students are (name, email, sessions, links) | `students/roster.generated.md` — regenerate, never hand-edit |\\r\\n| Learned facts and preferences (automemory) | native store `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-Joshu-dev-ai-os/memory/` + `MEMORY.md` index |\\r\\n| Skill / agent catalog | `skills/INDEX.md`, `agents/` |\\r\\n| Systems Jay 2 can reach (registry) | `connections.md` — 7 data domains, mechanism/auth/freshness; read by `/audit` |\\r\\n| Operator brain (how to think about automation) | `references/3ms-framework.md` — the Three Ms; walked weekly by `/level-up` |\\r\\n| Automation build backlog (what to build next, ranked) | `references/automation-backlog.md` — corpus-derived gaps + tiers; feeds `/level-up` |\\r\\n| How-it-works reference notes (methods, not state) | `references/` — also `references/claude-plus-codex.md`, `references/obsidian-command-center.md`, `references/second-brain-levels.md` |\\r\\n| Web research and Firecrawl agents | `references/firecrawl.md` (guidelines in `references/firecrawl/`) |\\r\\n| Shared Windows CLI tools for Codex, Claude Code, and Antigravity | `references/ai-workspace/windows-cli-toolchain.md` — installed paths, PATH refresh, and usage for `uv`, `yt-dlp`, FFmpeg, and Deno |\\r\\n| Immutable source evidence · intake queue | `raw/sources/` · `raw/inbox/` — one inbox, one archive |\\r\\n| Archived web clips, with provenance + hashes | `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/` — clip + `PROVENANCE.md` + `SHA256SUMS` |\\r\\n| Raw personal-data exports (Google Takeout, Gemini session transcripts) | `raw/data-about-me/` — unprocessed PII, git-ignored; never read wholesale |\\r\\n| Design/plan thinking, dated (grill-me + interview outputs) | `brainstorms/` — supersedes the retired `aios/` reform folder |\\r\\n| Session handoffs · chat exports | `handoffs/` — operational records, deliberately OUTSIDE `raw/`; `session-handoff` writes here |\\r\\n| Current local work in Claude/Codex cloud | `setup/github-sync/README.md`; private `codex/local-sync/<machine>/<checkout>` branches and generated `.cloud-sync/` metadata/conversation exports. Cloud edits use separate task branches. |\\r\\n| External teardowns and research, dated | `research/` |\\r\\n| Web-clipped articles (Obsidian Web Clipper) | `raw/inbox/` — intake queue; `ingest` copies and hash-verifies clips into `raw/sources/clips/`; processed originals stay until removal is authorized, so inbox presence alone does not mean unprocessed |\\r\\n| Application code | `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` — own repo, own instructions, own remote |\\r\\n| Other projects (life-path, …) | `../ai-os-projects/<name>/` — each with its own `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/` |\\r\\n\\r\\nApplication repositories and dependencies stay outside this Obsidian vault, in sibling `../ai-os-projects/`. Do not create a junction from the vault back into that directory.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Retrieval order\\r\\n\\r\\n1. `wiki/hot.md` — current-session narrative and open threads.\\r\\n2. `wiki/index.md` → the page (teaching knowledge: `corpus/index.md`; a student: their folder). Follow links; there is no semantic search and none is needed at this size.\\r\\n3. The live system — the final freshness escalation.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Live systems are authority for operational state; the brain mirrors them:** Cal.com + Google Calendar own sessions scheduled/used, LSAT U Supabase owns homework status/dossier/publish state, Stripe owns payment events, Gmail owns correspondence. On any disagreement, the backend wins. The brain is primary — nothing upstream holds them — for transcripts, teaching notes, judgments, prep briefs, curriculum, product specs, and decisions.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Do not read the wiki unless the task needs it.** Retrieval costs context every turn. Skip it for: code edits in `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/`; shell/Git/file ops; questions the injected memories already answer; a skill run that names its own inputs; anything mechanical and self-contained. Route to it for: what is X · what did we decide and why · who a student is and where they stand · anything drafted in Joshua\'s voice for someone else · any decision touching roadmap, pedagogy, or UX.\\r\\n\\r\\n**LLM Wiki schema:** For knowledge intake, knowledge questions, durable synthesis, and wiki maintenance, follow `system/schema/llm-wiki.md`. Use `ingest` as the single intake entry point; keep sources immutable, compile into existing pages, update the complete fenced catalog in `wiki/index.md`, and append changes to `wiki/log.md`. Preserve domain homes and live-system authority. Mechanical tasks retain the retrieval exceptions above.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Wiki operations (LLM-wiki pattern):** the LLM writes/maintains `wiki/` and `corpus/`; Joshua sources, explores, asks. Raw sources are immutable — read, never modify. *Ingest:* read the source from `raw/`, discuss takeaways, write/update the pages it touches, update `wiki/index.md`, append to `wiki/log.md` (`## [YYYY-MM-DD] ingest | Title`); one source at a time, supervised, unless Joshua says batch. *Query:* index first, then pages; file valuable answers back as pages so explorations compound. *Lint:* `second-brain-lint` for contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing pages.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Voice\\r\\n\\r\\n- **No em-dashes, ever.** Joshua never types them; a stray em-dash reads as AI and costs trust.\\r\\n- **No AI-slop vocabulary** — never \\"delve,\\" \\"tapestry,\\" \\"testament,\\" \\"demystify,\\" \\"boasts,\\" \\"in the realm of,\\" and their kin.\\r\\n- **Anything a student or prospect will read** routes through `wiki/teaching-voice.md` and is drafted, never sent, unless it is a pre-approved template.\\r\\n- **LSAT teaching:** use project-owned `lsat-u-voice` and `references/lsat-teaching-voice-standard.md`; this Joshua-selected standard takes precedence over older vendor voice blends.\\r\\n- **When an outbound message is authorized**, preserve the draft\'s paragraph breaks, list lines, and intentional spacing. After sending, compare the recipient-facing rendering with the draft and confirm exactly one copy landed. Report any mismatch; never resend automatically.\\r\\n- **Lead with your recommendation, not a menu.** Be decisive; don\'t over-hedge.\\r\\n- **Any prompt Joshua will paste elsewhere** goes inside a fenced code block, never inline prose.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tools, keys, and secrets\\r\\n\\r\\n- **The entire secret model is `.env` + `.gitignore`.** The root `.env` (git-ignored — verify with `git check-ignore .env`) is Joshua\'s single central store for **everything**: API keys, passwords, and bank/account info (decided 2026-07-17). OAuth client secrets live in `~/.config/gws/`, outside the repo. There is no vault, no Keychain, no encrypted store (`records.sparsebundle` is dead) and none is wanted. Never paste a credential into chat — add it to `.env` directly in the editor.\\r\\n- **Safety is the tool layer, not prompts:** allow/deny tool lists + scoped API keys. Jay 2 acts under its own credentials and never impersonates Joshua.\\r\\n- **Connected live systems:** Cal.com, Google Calendar, LSAT U Supabase, Stripe, Gmail. Full registry in `connections.md`.\\r\\n- **Google access is `gws` CLI only** (`gws gmail|drive|calendar|docs …`, keyring-auth; see `skills/codex/gws-shared/`). Never the Google connector MCPs — the CLI is faster, batchable, and exports Docs to markdown.\\r\\n- **Shared Windows command tools:** use `uv`, `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe`, `ffplay`, and `deno` from the Windows user PATH. For versions, locations, how to invoke them, or a stale terminal environment, read `references/ai-workspace/windows-cli-toolchain.md`. Check before reinstalling; restart the affected IDE when its inherited PATH is stale.\\r\\n- **Government IDs stay outside this OS.** Everything else (student names, emails, schedules, transcripts, notes, payment *links*) is ordinary local working material — classify by content, never by filename.\\r\\n- **Git remote is enabled.** `origin` is GitHub (`vnjkoxpl-42905/ai-os`, decided 2026-09-29). The outer repo never tracks `.env`, `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` (own repo), runtime logs, or locks. Do not create gitlinks.\\r\\n- **New laptop restore:** GitHub contains tracked ai-os files and skills. It deliberately excludes `.env`, `raw/`, app repos, credentials, and machine sessions. Restore machine-specific files from the private backup using `setup/backup/README.md` and its `README - START HERE.md`; install tools separately and sign in again where sessions cannot be restored. Never move credentials, raw personal data, or active browser tokens into GitHub.\\r\\n- **Authorized cloud transfer (2026-10-07):** private sync branches also carry portable skills, memory and conversation exports. Joshua explicitly authorized credential transfer; implementation uses the authenticated encrypted package described in `setup/github-sync/README.md`; plaintext secrets and its unlock key stay outside GitHub and Drive. Cloud authentication and native browser sessions still require separate verification.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Skills\\r\\n\\r\\nEverything is a skill — **there are no slash commands** (decided 2026-07-17: one kind, one home, one activation path). The catalog at `skills/` and `agents/` is inert storage; nothing auto-loads. An item runs only once **activated by copy** (not symlink) into `.agents/skills/` (Claude: `.claude/skills/`). Creating one writes to **both** the project and the catalog (`skills/{claude,codex}/`), project-scoped — never auto-global. `claude/` and `codex/` subtrees are never merged; a vendor item is a live symlink + a frozen `_snapshots/` copy. `system/scripts/check-skills.sh` validates the model; `skills/INDEX.md` indexes it.\\r\\n\\r\\nActive in this root. Run `pickup` only when Joshua explicitly asks for it. Do not run it automatically at session start. Use `wrapup` at the end of substantive sessions:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Skill | Use it when |\\r\\n|---|---|\\r\\n| `pickup` / `wrapup` | `pickup` only on Joshua\'s explicit request / `wrapup` at session end (wrapup persists to the wiki ledgers) |\\r\\n| `session-handoff` | mid-work context reset near ~250k, or passing work Codex↔Claude — chat-only, writes nothing |\\r\\n| `audit` | scoring the OS against the Four Cs (structural health, /100) |\\r\\n| `level-up` | weekly 3Ms interview to find + ship one automation |\\r\\n| `consultation-inquiry-drafts`, `-followup-drafts`, `inbound-tutoring-replies` | drafting to prospects/students — always via the teaching voice |\\r\\n| `guided-drill-assignment` | assigning a student a drill |\\r\\n| `lsat-u-platform-actions` | doing anything ON lsatprep.study from here (assign, post, message, ingest) |\\r\\n| `tutorocean-profile-fill` | TutorOcean profile work |\\r\\n| `prompt-architect-refiner` | refining a prompt before it ships |\\r\\n| `accommodations-email` | \\"accommodations email to X\\" (dictation: \\"accommodations scale\\"); pre-approved send, QP form attached, self-logging |\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen a skill run exposes a gap, improve the skill before moving on. Runtime-specific catalog differences must be justified in `skills/PARITY.md`; undeclared differences are defects.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Guardrails\\r\\n\\r\\n- **95% rule.** Make no changes until you are 95% confident what Joshua wants. Ask until you are.\\r\\n- **Lovable credits require confirmation.** Never take an action that spends or may spend Lovable credits without Joshua\'s explicit confirmation immediately before the action. Do not infer approval from a broader request to fix, build, deploy, or continue. Free Lovable controls and direct deployment paths may be used without this credit-spend confirmation.\\r\\n- **Lovable Cloud deploys through Lovable.** LSAT U currently uses a Lovable Cloud-managed backend. Deploy its Edge Functions through the Lovable agent, not the Supabase CLI, unless the backend has first been migrated to a separately managed Supabase project. Confirm this route with Joshua before starting a Lovable deployment.\\r\\n- **Root stays thin.** Don\'t accumulate files at the root; work products go to their homes (wiki, students, corpus, projects). Anything left at root gets filed before the session ends.\\r\\n- **Delegate bulk work.** Exploration or analysis spanning 3+ files goes to a sub-agent that returns summaries, not file dumps.\\r\\n- **Shell ergonomics.** Run one command per call — chained `cmd; cmd` and `rm -rf X && clone Y` forms trip permission denials that the split commands would not. Never poll with `sleep`. Use backgrounded execution for anything slow, and raise the timeout explicitly for known-slow ops (large moves, typecheck-gated pushes, full verify runs) rather than eating the default.\\r\\n- **Search before creating.** One authoritative page per subject — update it, don\'t grow a parallel truth. `wiki/index.md` catalogs every page and updates on every ingest.\\r\\n- **Preserve provenance and source hashes.** Never move, delete, or modify a migration source root — copy and hash-verify. Never follow a source symlink outside its registered root.\\r\\n- **Conflicts stay explicit until adjudicated** — never silently overwrite one source generation with another.\\r\\n- **Automation writes only generated files or fenced generated sections,** through compare-and-swap.\\r\\n- **Obey nested instruction files** — they win over broader ones for their subtree. LSATU\'s recovered `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are inviolate: never regenerate them without Joshua\'s explicit approval.\\r\\n- **Memory = native automemory.** \\"Remember that…\\" writes one fact per file to the native store; `MEMORY.md` indexes it. This file is the rules; memory is learned facts — never mix them. Transcripts and raw captures never auto-promote.\\r\\n- **Append meaningful system changes** to `wiki/log.md`; log locked decisions to `decisions/log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Dual-runtime (Codex + Claude)\\r\\n\\r\\n- Begin at the Git-root `AGENTS.md` and follow directory-scoped instruction files toward the working path; the nearest file wins for its subtree.\\r\\n- Keep root instructions inside the runtime byte budget. Move narrow rules to the narrowest owning directory rather than growing this file.\\r\\n- Activated skills are **copies** in `.agents/skills/` (from `skills/codex/`); agent definitions convert to `.codex/agents/*.toml` with the instructions in `developer_instructions`.\\r\\n- Claude reads `CLAUDE.md` and never this file. Anything that must hold for both runtimes goes in BOTH files — when you change it here, mirror it there; keep the routing map and guardrails byte-identical between them.\\r\\n- Activation is unequal by design: Codex reads copies in `.agents/skills/`, Claude reads copies in `.claude/skills/`. Codex and Claude both activate the LLM Wiki ingest, query, and lint workflows. Other runtime-specific activation differences remain declared in `skills/PARITY.md`. Never have separate runtimes writing the same page concurrently.\\r\\n- Never have Claude and Codex editing the same file at once; pass work between them by session handoff (summarize → clear → paste). At ~250k tokens, hand off rather than riding autocompact.\\r\\n"}'}]

This skill is self-contained and does not start Claudex Loop, require a formal plan, or create review logs.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Understand the job\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the current conversation and just enough relevant project context to identify the host, current model when known, desired outcome, and constraints. Implement real working code with exceptional attention to aesthetic details and creative choices.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user provides frontend requirements: a component, page, application, or interface to build. They may include context about the purpose, audience, or technical constraints.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Design Thinking\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore coding, understand the context and commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction:\\r\\n- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?\\r\\n- **Tone**: Pick an extreme: brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic/natural, luxury/refined, playful/toy-like, editorial/magazine, brutalist/raw, art deco/geometric, soft/pastel, industrial/utilitarian, etc. There are so many flavors to choose from. Use these for inspiration but design one that is true to the aesthetic direction.\\r\\n- **Constraints**: Technical requirements (framework, performance, accessibility).\\r\\n- **Differentiation**: What makes this UNFORGETTABLE? What\'s the one thing someone will remember?\\r\\n\\r\\n**CRITICAL**: Choose a clear conceptual direction and execute it with precision. Bold maximalism and refined minimalism both work - the key is intentionality, not intensity.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen implement working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue, etc.) that is:\\r\\n- Production-grade and functional\\r\\n- Visually striking and memorable\\r\\n- Cohesive with a clear aesthetic point-of-view\\r\\n- Meticulously refined in every detail\\r\\n\\r\\n## Frontend Aesthetics Guidelines\\r\\n\\r\\nFocus on:\\r\\n- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend\'s aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.\\r\\n- **Color & Theme**: Commit to a cohesive aesthetic. Use CSS variables for consistency. Dominant colors with sharp accents outperform timid, evenly-distributed palettes.\\r\\n- **Motion**: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only solutions for HTML. Use Motion library for React when available. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions. Use scroll-triggering and hover states that surprise.\\r\\n- **Spatial Composition**: Unexpected layouts. Asymmetry. Overlap. Diagonal flow. Grid-breaking elements. Generous negative space OR controlled density.\\r\\n- **Backgrounds & Visual Details**: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Add contextual effects and textures that match the overall aesthetic. Apply creative forms like gradient meshes, noise textures, geometric patterns, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, decorative borders, custom cursors, and grain overlays.\\r\\n\\r\\nNEVER use generic AI-generated aesthetics like overused font families (Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts), cliched color schemes (particularly purple gradients on white backgrounds), predictable layouts and component patterns, and cookie-cutter design that lacks context-specific character.\\r\\n\\r\\nInterpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. No design should be the same. Vary between light and dark themes, different fonts, different aesthetics. NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations.\\r\\n\\r\\n**IMPORTANT**: Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision. Maximalist designs need elaborate code with extensive animations and effects. Minimalist or refined designs need restraint, precision, and careful attention to spacing, typography, and subtle details. Elegance comes from executing the vision well.\\r\\n\\r\\nRemember: Claude is capable of extraordinary creative work. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 8.2 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Warning: truncated output (original token count: 20796)\nTotal output lines: 1\n\n{"chunk_id":"2d79e4","wall_time_seconds":1.0014263,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":20028,"output":"\\r\\nFILE C:\\\\Users\\\\Joshu\\\\dev\\\\ai-os\\\\skills\\\\codex\\\\higgsfield-generate\\\\SKILL.md\\r\\n---\\r\\nversion: 0.12.0\\r\\nname: higgsfield-generate\\r\\ndescription: |\\r\\n  Generate images/videos/3D assets/audio via Higgsfield AI. Defaults:\\r\\n  GPT Image 2 for image/design/text, Seedance 2.0 for\\r\\n  video, Nano Banana 2/Lite/Pro for character/reference\\r\\n  images, Marketing Studio for ads, Seed Audio 1.0 for audio.\\r\\n  Use when: \\"generate an image\\", \\"make a video\\", \\"animate\\r\\n  this photo\\", \\"image-to-video\\", \\"edit/stylize/remix this\\r\\n  image\\", \\"reframe this video\\", \\"edit this video from a\\r\\n  sketch\\", \\"create a 3D model/GLB\\", \\"create a sound effect\\",\\r\\n  \\"make music\\", \\"text-to-audio\\", \\"create an ad\\", \\"make a UGC\\r\\n  video\\", \\"unboxing\\", \\"presenter video\\", \\"import product from\\r\\n  URL\\", or \\"analyze video virality\\". Supports image-to-3D\\r\\n  (`multi_image_to_3d`),\\r\\n  text-to-audio/music (`seed_audio`), workflow generation\\r\\n  (`draw_to_video`, `reframe`), Marketing Studio, and\\r\\n  Virality Predictor (`brain_activity`).\\r\\n  Chain with higgsfield-soul-id for face/identity consistency.\\r\\n  NOT for: Soul Character training (use higgsfield-soul-id),\\r\\n  product photoshoots, marketplace listing cards,\\r\\n  text/chat/TTS tasks.\\r\\nargument-hint: \\"[prompt-or-analysis-request] [--model <name>] [--image|--video <path-or-id>]\\"\\r\\nallowed-tools: Bash\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Higgsfield Generate\\r\\n\\r\\nSubmit jobs to any Higgsfield model. Wraps the `higgsfield` CLI. Covers generic image/video/3D/audio generation, Marketing Studio (branded ads, avatars, products, hooks, settings), and, secondarily, Virality Predictor video scoring.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Step 0 — Bootstrap\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore any other command:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. If `higgsfield` is not on `$PATH`, install it:\\r\\n   ```bash\\r\\n   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/higgsfield-ai/cli/main/install.sh | sh\\r\\n   ```\\r\\n2. If `higgsfield account status` fails with `Session expired` / `Not authenticated`, ask the user to run `higgsfield auth login` (interactive) and wait for confirmation.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n## UX Rules\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Be concise. No raw IDs, no JSON dumps in chat. Print the media URL for generated assets, or the text summary for Virality Predictor.\\r\\n2. No internal jargon. Don\'t narrate \\"calling higgsfield cost\\", \\"polling job\\".\\r\\n3. Detect the user\'s language from the first message and reply in it. Technical args (`--aspect_ratio 16:9`) stay English.\\r\\n4. Don\'t batch-ask. Pick a sane default model and ask one thing at a time only if genuinely missing.\\r\\n5. Don\'t pre-estimate cost or optimize for cheaper models unless the user asks. Prefer the quality default first.\\r\\n6. Pass `--wait` to `generate create` so the command blocks until done and prints the result URL itself. Avoid the two-step `create` → `wait` pattern.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Discovery guardrail\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen looking for a Higgsfield feature/model, do not rely only on semantic search or CLI `--help`. First run an unfiltered model list, then inspect likely `job_set_type` names. If the user says a model exists but search returns no results, trust that signal and verify with the full model list before answering.\\r\\n\\r\\nWorkflows are separate from models. Discover them with `higgsfield workflow list` and inspect params with `higgsfield workflow get <workflow_name>`.\\r\\n\\r\\nVirality Predictor is exposed as:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Customer-facing name: Virality Predictor\\r\\n- Technical `job_set_type`: `brain_activity`\\r\\n- Category/output: text report. This is video-in/text-out analysis, not a text/chat generation model.\\r\\n- Input: uploaded video\\r\\n- Purpose: finished-video hook, attention, retention, and virality analysis\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the user says \\"analyze this video\\", \\"score this ad\\", \\"evaluate the hook\\", or similar, route to `brain_activity` even though it appears under text/analysis models. Classify by task intent and required input, not by output category alone.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Workflow — generic generation\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Pick a model.** Start with the core defaults unless the brief clearly needs a specialist:\\r\\n\\r\\n   - **GPT Image 2** → default image model for high-fidelity general generation, graphic design, UI, banners, typography, and on-image text.\\r\\n   - **Seedance 2.0** → default video model for serious motion, cinematic clips, multi-shot work, image-to-video, and 4–15s production-quality output up to 4K. 12s is valid.\\r\\n   - **Nano Banana 2/Lite/Pro** → default for character, cartoon, stylized, and reference-driven image work; use Lite for speed/cost, Pro for harder briefs.\\r\\n   - **Marketing Studio** → default for ads, UGC, product demos, unboxing, TV spots, presenter videos, and brand/product workflows.\\r\\n   - **Seed Audio 1.0** → default audio model for text-to-audio, voice, sound effects, ambience, foley, and music-like audio unless the user names Sonilo/Mirelo.\\r\\n\\r\\n   **Image:**\\r\\n   - Brand product visual (Pinterest pin, lifestyle, hero banner, ad pack, virtual try-on) → use `higgsfield-product-photoshoot` instead. NOT this skill.\\r\\n   - Generated product concept / packaging / can / bottle with brand name or label text → GPT Image 2.\\r\\n   - Branded ad image with avatar + product (Marketing Studio shape) → Marketing Studio Image (see Marketing Studio below)\\r\\n   - Aesthetic UGC / fashion editorial / lifestyle character → Soul 2.0\\r\\n   - Cinematic still frame → Soul Cinema\\r\\n   - Highly characterful creative persona (text-only, distinctive) → Soul Cast\\r\\n   - Locations / environments / no-people scenes → Soul Location (best in class)\\r\\n   - Logo, icon, vector-like illustration, brand mark, controlled-palette graphic → Recraft V4.1 (`recraft_v4_1`, often with `--model_type vector`)\\r\\n   - Face edit + complex scene swap → Seedream 4.5\\r\\n   - Soul Character (reference id from `higgsfield-soul-id`) → Soul 2.0 for stills, Soul Cinema for cinematic\\r\\n   - Character or cartoon-style work → Nano Banana 2; use Nano Banana 2 Lite (`nano_banana_2_lite`) for fast/simple reference edits, step up to Nano Banana Pro on hard cases\\r\\n   - Fast and cheap iteration → Z Image\\r\\n   - **Default for everything else → GPT Image 2.** Graphic design, UI, banners, typography, and high-fidelity general generation.\\r\\n\\r\\n   **Video:**\\r\\n   - All advertising / commercial / branded ad video → Marketing Studio (see Marketing Studio below)\\r\\n   - Edit existing video from sketch/timestamp, or reframe to another aspect ratio → workflow (`draw_to_video` or `reframe`), not a model. See `references/workflows.md`.\\r\\n   - **Default all-purpose serious video (multi-shot, consistent identity, motion-heavy, image-to-video, 4–15s requests) → Seedance 2.0.** SOTA. Do not downgrade to Seedance 1.5 just because its duration enum is easier to read; validate Seedance 2.0 first.\\r\\n   - Single-plane scene without strong dynamics, cheaper than Seedance 2.0 → Kling 3.0; if the user explicitly asks for Turbo, faster, or lower-cost Kling output → Kling 3.0 Turbo (`kling3_0_turbo`)\\r\\n   - Cheap clean shot without cuts, only when the user asks for cheaper/budget output → Seedance 1.5 Pro\\r\\n   - Cinema-grade highest fidelity → Cinema Studio Video 3.0\\r\\n   - Cheap with strong physics, no audio needed → Minimax Hailuo\\r\\n   - Fast batch / volume → Veo 3.1 Lite\\r\\n   - Bold/stylized image-to-video from a required start image → Grok Video 1.5 (`grok_video_v15`). Requires one `--start-image` or `--image`, duration 2–15s, resolution `480p` or `720p`.\\r\\n   - Multimodal reference-to-video with up to 7 images or one video reference → Gemini Omni Flash (`gemini_omni`); keep Seedance 2.0 as the default serious-video pick.\\r\\n\\r\\n   **Video analysis:**\\r\\n   - Rate a finished video\'s hook, virality potential, attention, retention, or distraction risk → Virality Predictor (`brain_activity`). This is a video analysis model that returns a text score/report, not a generated media asset.\\r\\n\\r\\n   **3D:**\\r\\n   - Create an actual 3D mesh/model/GLB from one or more object/product reference images → Multi-Image to 3D (`multi_image_to_3d`). Pass 1–4 images with repeated `--image`; use `--should_texture true` when the asset needs texture. If the user only asks for a 3D-rendered picture, use an image model instead.\\r\\n\\r\\n   **Audio:**\\r\\n   - **Default for audio generation → Seed Audio 1.0 (`seed_audio`).** Use for text-to-audio, sound effects, ambience, foley, impacts, environmental audio, voice-style generations, and music-like audio. It requires `--prompt`; use optional `--audio-references`/`--image-references` only when the user provides references.\\r\\n   - Use Sonilo Music (`sonilo_music`) only when the user explicitly asks for Sonilo or you need that specialist music model. It requires `--prompt` and `--duration`, and returns audio.\\r\\n   - Use Mirelo Text to Audio (`mirelo_text_to_audio`) only when the user explicitly asks for Mirelo or you need that legacy SFX model. It requires `--prompt` and `--duration`, and returns audio.\\r\\n\\r\\n   For the actual `--model` ID to pass to `higgsfield generate create`, run `higgsfield model list --json | jq` to map display names to IDs. See `references/model-catalog.md` for the full table.\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **Pass media inputs straight to flags.** Media flags accept a local file path **or** a UUID. CLI auto-uploads paths and auto-detects job vs upload for UUIDs. No need to pre-upload. Each model declares accepted media roles or `*_references` params — see `references/media-inputs.md`.\\r\\n3. **Validate quickly.** If unsure of params, run `higgsfield model get <jst> --json` once and pass only what\'s needed. Validate the preferred model before falling back to an older one. Use schema defaults otherwise. The server returns `adjustments` for non-fatal coercions (e.g. `aspect_ratio=99:99` → closest match) and a structured error for invalid declared-param values.\\r\\n4. **Submit and wait in one shot.** `higgsfield generate create <jst> [--prompt \\"...\\"] [media flags] [param flags] --wait`. Blocks until terminal status and prints the result on stdout. Tunables: `--wait-timeout 20m` (default 10m), `--wait-interval 5s` (default 3s). Virality Predictor does not need a prompt; pass `--video`.\\r\\n5. **Deliver.** For generated media and 3D assets, send the primary result URL plus a one-line summary (model, duration if video; GLB/asset URL for 3D). For Virality Predictor, deliver the scores, business interpretation, and the Open report link. Do not surface Virality Predictor `.glb`, `.bin`, or region-table internals in normal chat output.\\r\\n\\r\\nTo inspect or rerun later, `higgsfield generate list --json` and `higgsfield generate get <id> --json` work for retrospection. `higgsfield generate wait <id>` is still available if you ever need to rejoin a job started without `--wait`.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor workflow jobs, use `higgsfield generate workflow <workflow_name> ... --wait`. Cost syntax is `higgsfield generate cost workflow <workflow_name> ...`. See `references/workflows.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Media flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Purpose | Models that accept it |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| `--image <path-or-id>` | reference image | most image models, `grok_video_v15`, `multi_image_to_3d`, `seedance_2_0`, `veo3`, `marketing_studio_video` |\\r\\n| `--start-image <path-or-id>` | first frame for image-to-video transitions | `grok_video_v15`, `kling3_0`, `kling3_0_turbo`, `kling2_6`, `veo3_1`, `seedance_2_0`, `marketing_studio_video` |\\r\\n| `--end-image <path-or-id>` | last frame for transitions | `kling3_0`, `seedance_2_0`, `marketing_studio_video` |\\r\\n| `--video <path-or-id>` | reference or analyzed video | `seedance_2_0`, `brain_activity` |\\r\\n| `--audio <path-or-id>` | reference audio (lipsync, soundtrack match) | `seedance_2_0` (use this, NOT `--generate-audio`) |\\r\\n\\r\\nFor reference-array models, the explicit flags are `--image-references`, `--video-references`, and `--audio-references`; `--image`, `--video`, and `--audio` are short aliases when the schema exposes those params.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach flag accepts either a local file path (auto-uploaded) or a UUID (upload id from `higgsfield upload create`, or a previous job id). Each model declares its own media roles or `*_references` params. See `references/media-inputs.md` for the full table.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Common params\\r\\n\\r\\nFlags pass through to model schema. Use `higgsfield model get <jst>` to discover.\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create gpt_image_2 --prompt \\"neon city at dusk\\" --aspect_ratio 16:9 --resolution 2k --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create nano_banana_2 --prompt \\"anime character concept, expressive pose\\" --image ./ref.png --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create seedance_2_0 --prompt \\"camera dollies in\\" --start-image ./first.png --duration 12 --resolution 4k --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create grok_video_v15 --prompt \\"cinematic handheld shot, neon rainy street\\" --start-image ./image.png --duration 5 --resolution 720p --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create text2image_soul_v2 --prompt \\"...\\" --soul-id <soul_ref_id> --quality 2k --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create multi_image_to_3d --image ./front.png --image ./side.png --should_texture true --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create seed_audio --prompt \\"cinematic rain ambience with distant thunder\\" --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create sonilo_music --prompt \\"cinematic synthwave track\\" --duration 12 --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create mirelo_text_to_audio --prompt \\"glass breaking in a large hall\\" --duration 4 --wait\\r\\nhiggsfield generate create brain_activity --video ./ad.mp4 --wait\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nFor machine-readable output (chained pipelines, agent context), add `--json`. With `--wait --json` you get the final job object array. Without `--wait`, you get the job IDs. Virality Predictor stores raw analysis and render artifacts in the job params, but the default text output should stay to scores plus Open report.\\r\\n\\r\\nStdin prompt: `echo \\"...\\" | higgsfield generate create z_image --wait`.\\r\\n\\r\\nSoul image quality: for `text2image_soul_v2` and `soul_cinematic`, pass `--quality 1.5k` or `--quality 2k`. These are UI-facing tiers; the backend maps them to `720p`/`1080p` and model-specific dimensions from the selected `--aspect_ratio`. `soul_location` has no quality selector; it uses fixed dimensions per aspect ratio.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Marketing Studio\\r\\n\\r\\nBranded image/video gen: avatars + products + optional setup hooks/settings + ad-style modes. Use models `marketing_studio_video` and `marketing_studio_image`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Concepts\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Avatar** — presenter face. Curated `preset` (browse `higgsfield marketing-studio avatars list`) or `custom` (uploaded photos via `higgsfield marketing-studio avatars create`). For UGC modes, an avatar is optional if the brief clearly mentions a person; the backend can create a Soul Character automatically. Pass an avatar when the user wants a specific presenter.\\r\\n- **Product** — brand item with title + reference images. Imported from URL (`higgsfield marketing-studio products fetch --url ...`) or created from uploaded images (`higgsfield marketing-studio products create`).\\r\\n- **Webproduct** — App Store / web page version. Auto-routes when fetching App Store URLs.\\r\\n- **Hook** — reusable opening angle / ad hook. Browse with `higgsfield marketing-studio hooks list`. Hook text is prepended to the user\'s prompt; it does not replace `--prompt`.\\r\\n- **Setting** — reusable environment / scene context. Browse with `higgsfield marketing-studio settings list`.\\r\\n- **Ad reference** — reusable inspiration video that can be bound to an avatar and/or product. Created from an uploaded video (`--video-input <upload_id>`) or a previous generation job (`--job <job_id>`). Browse with `higgsfield marketing-studio ad-references list`. See `references/marketing-ad-references.md`.\\r\\n- **Brand kit** — captures a brand\'s identity (name, logo, hero images, colours, fonts, tone) for reuse across image generations. Created by handing in a website URL (`higgsfield marketing-studio brand-kits fetch --url https://… --wait`). See `references/marketing-brand-kits.md`.\\r\\n- **Ad format** — presets that drives the visual structure of a generated image (`headline`, `bullet-points`, etc.). Read-only, browse with `higgsfield marketing-studio ad-formats list`. Required input for `dtc-ads generate`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Discovery commands\\r\\n\\r\\nUse these exact list commands when the user asks what already exists:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nhiggsfield marketing-studio avatars list --json\\r\\nhiggsfield marketing-studio products list --json\\r\\nhiggsfield marketing-studio hooks list --json\\r\\nhiggsfield marketing-studio settings list --json\\r\\nhiggsfield marketing-studio ad-references list --json\\r\\nhiggsfield marketing-studio brand-kits list --json\\r\\nhiggsfield marketing-studio ad-formats list --json\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n`--hook_id` and `--setting_id` are supported by `marketing_studio_video` only; do not pass them to `marketing_studio_image`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### UX rules (additional)\\r\\n\\r\\n- One question per phase. Don\'t ask product+avatar+mode upfront.\\r\\n- **Two ad approaches are mutually exclusive.** Either the user gives an ad reference video (reference-driven) **or** picks hook/setting blocks (composed-from-blocks) — never both. If the user has an ad reference selected, do not offer hook/setting; if hook/setting are picked, do not offer to attach an ad reference.\\r\\n- **Ad reference source.** The only valid inputs are a local video file (uploaded via `higgsfield upload create ... --video`) or a prior video job. If the user provides anything else, ask for a local file.\\r\\n- **`dtc-ads` ad format is mandatory.** Always ask the user to pick from `ad-formats list`. There is no auto-default — both the CLI and server reject calls without `--format-id`.\\r\\n- **`dtc-ads` optional inputs.** Suggest avatars, products, and reference media when the brief calls for them; only attach what the user picks.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Workflow — quick ad video\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Get product.**\\r\\n   - Existing product → `higgsfield marketing-studio products list --json`\\r\\n   - URL → `higgsfield marketing-studio products fetch --url <url> --wait` (polls until import done)\\r\\n   - Local images → `higgsfield upload create <photo>...` then `higgsfield marketing-studio products create --title \\"...\\" --image <id>...`\\r\\n   Capture product id. Use built-in `image_gen` with chroma-key removal first for simple opaque subjects; ask before using CLI true transparency for complex subjects.\\r\\n- style-transfer — apply reference style while changing subject/scene.\\r\\n- compositing — multi-image insert/merge with matched lighting/perspective.\\r\\n- sketch-to-render — drawing/line art to photoreal render.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Shared prompt schema\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the following labeled spec as shared prompt scaffolding for both top-level modes:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nUse case: <taxonomy slug>\\r\\nAsset type: <where the asset will be used>\\r\\nPrimary request: <user\'s main prompt>\\r\\nInput images: <Image 1: role; Image 2: role> (optional)\\r\\nScene/backdrop: <environment>\\r\\nSubject: <main subject>\\r\\nStyle/medium: <photo/illustration/3D/etc>\\r\\nComposition/framing: <wide/close/top-down; placement>\\r\\nLighting/mood: <lighting + mood>\\r\\nColor palette: <palette notes>\\r\\nMaterials/textures: <surface details>\\r\\nText (verbatim): \\"<exact text>\\"\\r\\nConstraints: <must keep/must avoid>\\r\\nAvoid: <negative constraints>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nNotes:\\r\\n- `Asset type` and `Input images` are prompt scaffolding, not dedicated CLI flags.\\r\\n- `Scene/backdrop` refers to the visual setting. keep the product and its edges unchanged; no text; no watermark\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Prompting best practices\\r\\n- Structure prompt as scene/backdrop -> subject -> details -> constraints.\\r\\n- Include intended use (ad, UI mock, infographic) to set the mode and polish level.\\r\\n- Use camera/composition language for photorealism.\\r\\n- Only use SVG/vector stand-ins when the user explicitly asked for vector output or a non-image placeholder.\\r\\n- Quote exact text and specify typography + placement.\\r\\n- For tricky words, spell them letter-by-letter and require verbatim rendering.\\r\\n- For multi-image inputs, reference images by index and describe how they should be used.\\r\\n- For edits, repeat invariants every iteration to reduce drift.\\r\\n- Iterate with single-change follow-ups.\\r\\n- If the prompt is generic, add only the extra detail that will materially help.\\r\\n- If the prompt is already detailed, normalize it instead of expanding it.\\r\\n- For CLI fallback only, see `references/cli.md` and `references/image-api.md` for model, `quality`, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, and output-path guidance.\\r\\n- For transparent images, use the built-in-first chroma-key workflow unless the request is complex enough to need true CLI transparency; Run the LSAT U steps from an LSAT U checkout on its own branch (never the main checkout another session may be using), and ship bank changes as a PR.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Two sources, pick by need\\r\\n\\r\\n| Need | Source | Login |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| Difficulty, question type, features, reasoning type for all 10,171 LSAT Lab questions | `app.lsatlab.com/my/services/get-questions-just-props.php` + `/api/question-properties`, fetched inside a logged-in tab | Yes |\\r\\n| Full question and answer-choice text, answer key, and written explanations for one question | `app.lsatlab.com/api/questions/<id>`, using `qid` from `data/questions-props.json` | Yes |\\r\\n| Answer key, answer %, trap labels, written explanation, question text, first words of each choice, each test\'s question list | public pages `www.lsatlab.com/lsat-explanations/PT<n>-S<s>-Q<q>` via `crawl_public.py` | No |\\r\\n\\r\\nThe public pages cut choices short. Use the logged-in `/api/questions/<id>` response\'s `answers[]` for full choice text; the official PrepTest PDFs Joshua keeps in Downloads are another source for adjudicating a disagreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Refresh the logged-in data (only when tags may have changed)\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a logged-in Codex browser tab, or skip this step and use the existing data/ files. Crawl the public pages\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython <vault>/system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/crawl_public.py            # every LR slot in the bank\\r\\npython <vault>/system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/crawl_public.py --pts 113  # one test\\r\\n```\\r\\n~4,000 pages, 6 workers, resumable (skips slots already in `data/public/`). Pull the database (read-only)\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/db_pull.py   # from the vault root; writes data/db/\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Audit\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython <vault>/system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/audit_bank.py --db <vault>/system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/data/db --out <report.md>\\r\\n```\\r\\nFindings: `key_mismatch` (bank / database / LSAT Lab disagree), `stimulus_not_on_lsatlab` / `stem_not_on_lsatlab` / `choice_not_on_lsatlab` (wrong or damaged question text), `db_stimulus_not_on_lsatlab`, `in_lsatlab_not_in_bank` / `in_bank_not_in_lsatlab_list` (missing or extra slots), `lsatlab_explained_lsatu_not` (LSAT Lab has a written explanation where LSAT U\'s Coverage State is not Complete), `labels_differ`.\\r\\n\\r\\nRead a sample of every finding type before reporting it.
