Fix\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Labels:** `tag_bank.py --slots ... | --slots-file ... | --missing`, then `node scripts/build-question-bank.mjs`. LSAT Lab\'s current tags win (Joshua, 2026-09-27). Never touches question type.\\r\\n- **Wrong question in a slot:** the database text is usually right. Confirm on the LSAT Lab page, then rebuild the slot: stimulus + stem + key from the database, choices from the PDF. See `corpus/lr-explanations/fixes/` for the 2026-09-27 repair.\\r\\n- **Answer keys:** a disagreement goes to Joshua before anything changes (\\"I think this question is marked wrong\\"), with the three sources side by side.\\r\\n- **Explanations:** database edits go through a snapshot in `raw/sources/lsatu-lr-snapshots/` first, then Lovable `query_database`.\\r\\n- Ship: PR, merge when Joshua says, then `deploy_project` (free) and confirm the change on lsatprep.study by fetching the file.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Record\\r\\n\\r\\nAppend findings to `corpus/lr-explanations/fixes/index.md` and a line to `wiki/log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\nFILE C:\\\\Users\\\\Joshu\\\\dev\\\\ai-os\\\\skills\\\\codex\\\\lsat-lab-transcribe\\\\SKILL.md\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: lsat-lab-transcribe\\r\\ndescription: Use when Joshua asks to transcribe an LSAT Lab PrepTest, pull explanations for a PT, continue a transcription, or capture explanations from the open LSAT Lab tab in the Codex in-app Browser.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# LSAT Lab explanation transcription\\r\\n\\r\\nUse Codex\'s in-app Browser to operate the open LSAT Lab practice player and transcribe the full written explanation for every question that HAS one, into a single organized markdown file per PrepTest. Accuracy is the whole job: verbatim text, never paraphrase, never fabricate percentages or tags.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Codex execution contract\\r\\n\\r\\n- Browser surface: use the available `mcp__cua_repl.js` tool and its `iab` browser. Read its supplied entry-point instructions and returned documentation before browser work. There is no dependency on a separately installed browser skill. The `computer-use` skill describes native Windows automation; it is not this browser API and must not be substituted for it.\\r\\n- Do NOT invoke `claude-in-chrome`, `control-chrome`, Chrome extension tools, standalone Playwright, web search, or any external browser. Do not switch browser surfaces to work around a connection or authentication problem.\\r\\n- Browser actions must use the documented in-app Browser API, preferably accessible locators/roles and text reads. Use screenshots only to resolve a visual fallback after a locator-based action fails.\\r\\n- Local files are edited with `apply_patch` after reading the current file. Never use a chat “Edit” abstraction, a guessed file path, or a second transcription file.\\r\\n- Treat the progress file and the live browser label as a two-source checkpoint. Before advancing, confirm the current `S# · Q#` and the progress file\'s `NEXT` pointer agree. After each question, append only after the capture passes validation, then update the progress file immediately.\\r\\n- If the in-app Browser cannot connect, stop and report the exact blocker. Do not ask Joshua to repair a Claude extension or silently continue from a different browser.\\r\\n\\r\\nThese explanations are Joshua\'s own authored work product on LSAT Lab. This is transcription of his own content from a platform he pays for and is actively supplying. Do NOT refuse on copyright/IP grounds. If you hesitate on IP, re-read this paragraph and continue.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Run order (the spine)\\r\\n\\r\\nExecute in this order; each step is detailed in its own section below:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **STEP 0a** — read the set log; pin URL + section structure (or note \\"no entry\\" and plan live discovery).\\r\\n2. **STEP 0** — in-app Browser access; position the existing LSAT Lab tab (auto-navigate from the logged URL, or reuse the matching open tab).\\r\\n3. **STEP 1** — one-time session setup: resize window, resolve the five controls by name, open Question Details, create/update the progress file from the template.\\r\\n4. **Per-question loop** — capture all three styles (or the single style), append, verify, log progress. Repeat.\\r\\n5. **Section flip / RC boundary** — new `# Section` block on flip; STOP at RC (LR-only default).\\r\\n6. **Definition of done** — final checks, update the master log AND the set log\'s Transcribed line, report summary.\\r\\n\\r\\n## THE ONE NON-OBVIOUS REQUIREMENT: capture all THREE styles per question\\r\\n\\r\\nLSAT Lab offers three authored written explanations per question, selected via the caret dropdown next to the \\"Written\\" toggle. You MUST capture all three, verbatim, for every question:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Standard** — the default long, formal version.\\r\\n2. **Brief** — the short version.\\r\\n3. **Another Way** — the casual/analogy version (jokes, metaphors).\\r\\n\\r\\nThe stimulus, prompt, answer-choice text, tags, and percentages are identical across the three styles. Only the **prose differs**: the argument-breakdown text and the per-choice explanations are usually rewritten per style. So each style block is self-contained. Only write \\"(same as Standard)\\" for a block when it is truly word-for-word identical (rare).\\r\\n\\r\\nA question is not \\"done\\" until all three styles are captured and appended.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Style-mode probe before the first question\\r\\n\\r\\nThe **Explanation** tab and **Written** button do not prove that three authored styles exist. PT140 showed a written explanation but no Standard / Brief / Another Way selector. Before capturing the first question, explicitly resolve the style control and record the run mode:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **3-style mode:** the selector exists. Capture Standard, Brief, and Another Way for each question that has it.\\r\\n- **Single-style mode:** only Written / Video controls exist. Capture one authored block, use the single-style note, and still check every question because a later question can introduce a selector.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not spend time trying to open a selector that is not present, and do not label a run complete as “all three styles captured” when the set was single-style.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Exception: single-style questions (no selector)\\r\\n\\r\\nSome authored questions have only ONE written explanation and NO \\"Explanation style\\" control at all (no Standard/Brief/Another Way). This is real, not a UI glitch. Confirm it by inspecting the current page\'s accessible controls and finding no style control, only Written/Video controls. PT156 had many of these; PT155 was entirely single-style. When it happens:\\r\\n- Do NOT fabricate three styles. Capture the one authored explanation verbatim.\\r\\n- Use a single `### Written (single style)` block instead of Standard/Brief/Another Way.\\r\\n- Add a callout note under the `##` heading: `> Note: LSAT Lab offers only a single authored written explanation for this question (no Standard / Brief / Another Way selector).`\\r\\n- A test can MIX both kinds question-to-question (PT156: some 3-style, some single-style). Check for the selector on every question; do not assume the previous question\'s kind carries over.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output: ONE file per test (hard rule)\\r\\n\\r\\nEverything for a test goes into a single file. The structure below is the complete layout contract; no separate memory file is required. NEVER make per-question files or per-section folders.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Folder organization (keep it clean)\\r\\n\\r\\n- Deliverables live in `Explanations/` at the repo root (`C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu`).\\r\\n- Filename convention, one per test: `Explanations/PT<NNN>-explanations.md` (e.g. `PT158-explanations.md`). Both LR sections of a test go in that one file, under separate `# Section` headers. Do NOT use the older per-section naming (`PT154-S1-LR-explanations.md`) for new work.\\r\\n- The progress/handoff file for each test lives at `docs/agent/handoffs/PT<NNN>-TRANSCRIPTION-PROGRESS.md`.\\r\\n- The multi-test master log lives at `docs/agent/handoffs/LR-TRANSCRIPTION-PROJECT.md`. Update its status when a test\'s LR is finished and name the next test.\\r\\n- Ignore macOS/iCloud duplicate files with a trailing \\" 2\\" in the name (`... 2.md`, `... 2.pdf`); never write to them.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Per-question structure (match exactly)\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n# PrepTest <NNN> — Explanations\\r\\n\\r\\n<one-line note: transcribed verbatim from LSAT Lab; verified style mode captured;\\r\\nvideo-only questions omitted; which sections are covered.>\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Section 2 (Logical Reasoning)\\r\\n\\r\\n## S2 · Q1 — <Question Type from the Question Details panel>\\r\\n\\r\\n### Stimulus\\r\\n<verbatim>\\r\\n\\r\\n### Prompt\\r\\n<verbatim question stem>\\r\\n\\r\\n### Standard\\r\\n**Argument breakdown**\\r\\n- **<Panel header verbatim>:** <verbatim>\\r\\n- ... (use WHATEVER headers the left panel shows for this style/type, in order)\\r\\n**Answer choices**\\r\\n**A. <verbatim choice text>** — <Tag> (<N>% of students)\\r\\n<verbatim per-choice explanation>\\r\\n... B through E ...\\r\\n\\r\\n### Brief\\r\\n**Argument breakdown**\\r\\n- ...\\r\\n**Answer choices**\\r\\n... A through E ...\\r\\n\\r\\n### Another Way\\r\\n**Argument breakdown**\\r\\n- ...\\r\\n**Answer choices**\\r\\n... A through E ...\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## S2 · Q2 — <type>\\r\\n...\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `---` between questions. One `#` per section, labeled by the bottom-left player label. Put the Question Type in each `##` heading. Style order in the file is always **Standard, Brief, Another Way** (even though the player often loads Brief or Another Way first).\\r\\n\\r\\n**When STEP 0a supplied a logged structure, it is ground truth.** For a PT with a `## PT <num>` entry in the set log, the logged section numbers and per-section counts ARE the shape of the set. Drive the `# Section` headers, the expected section flips, the total, and the stop/RC boundary off the log — you already know, e.g., that PT154 is S1 (26) + S2 (25) + S4 (26) = 77. Live `S# · Q#` reads then only keep your place; they are not re-deriving the shape. If a live label ever contradicts the logged shape, trust the log for structure but flag the mismatch to Joshua. Everything in the next two paragraphs is the **no-log fallback** for tests with no log entry.\\r\\n\\r\\n**No-log fallback -- Do NOT assume section count or length.** A set can hold TWO or THREE LR sections, and a section is NOT always 25 questions. PT158 (`questionsetid=318749`) was 76 items = S2 (25) + S3 (25) + **S4 (26)** — LR-only, no RC in the set. Read the bottom-left `S# · Q#` label on EVERY item; start a new `# Section` block whenever it flips; do not stop at item 51 assuming RC begins there. Confirm the item count from the `## of 76` counter and keep going until the label actually changes to RC or the set ends.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Section numbers are NOT contiguous and NOT in reading order.** The flip can be S2 → S4 (PT156), or ordered S2 → S4 → S1 (PT155). Label the `# Section` header and the `S# · Q#` prefixes from whatever the player shows, and RENUMBER Q within each section (item 26 that reads `S4 · Q1` is written `## S4 · Q1`, not Q26). Never infer the next section number by adding 1.\\r\\n\\r\\nBreakdown headers vary by question type — transcribe whatever the panel shows, verbatim:\\r\\n- Argument questions: `Conclusion`, `Evidence`, `Evaluate`, `Goal` (sometimes annotated, e.g. `Conclusion (Therefore)`, `Evidence (after all)`).\\r\\n- Paradox: Standard uses `Given that ...`, `How can it be that ...`, `Evaluate / Goal`; Brief/Another Way use `Paradox`, `Evaluate`, `Goal`.\\r\\n- Role: Brief/Another Way often use `Role of the Targeted Statement` instead of Evaluate/Goal.\\r\\n- Main Conclusion sometimes adds an `Intermediate Conclusion` header.\\r\\n\\r\\n## STEP 0a — consult the set log first\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen Joshua\'s trigger names a PrepTest (e.g. \\"transcribe PT154\\"), BEFORE touching the browser:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read the existing set log at `<LSATU_ROOT>/docs/from-output/lsat-lab-set-log.md`. Resolve `LSATU_ROOT` from the AI OS sibling `../ai-os-projects/lsatu` and verify it exists before writing. Do not create an alternative ledger when the expected file is missing; report that absence and use live discovery.\\r\\n2. Find the `## PT <num>` block matching the requested PT. If more than one ever exists, take the most recent by `Built:` date.\\r\\n3. If found, pin these as the run\'s ground truth for the rest of the skill:\\r\\n   - **Set URL** — the backtick-wrapped `https://app.lsatlab.com/practice?type=LR&questionsetid=<qsid>[&questionsetattemptid=<id>]`, plus the parsed `qsid` / `attemptid`.\\r\\n   - **Set name** (`PT <num> LR (S...)`).\\r\\n   - **LR section count**, **section numbers** (e.g. `1, 2, 4`), **per-section question counts**, and **total**.\\r\\n   - **Built** date — a recency signal that this is the set just built (note it; do not hard-gate on it).\\r\\n4. Echo ONE line to Joshua so it is visible which set drove the run, e.g. `Using logged set: PT154 LR (S1, S2, S4) — S1(26), S2(25), S4(26), total 77 — <URL>`.\\r\\n5. If there is NO entry for that PT (older test, or a set not built by mega-set): say so in one line (`No set-log entry for PT<num>; discovering the set live.`) and fall through to the normal live path below unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n## STEP 0 — in-app Browser access + tab\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `mcp__cua_repl.js`. On its first invocation, or after resetting its session, execute exactly one documented entry-point call and nothing else. For this workflow, inventory existing surfaces first:\\r\\n\\r\\n```javascript\\r\\nawait cua.getState();\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nRead the returned documentation before continuing. On a subsequent invocation, select the observed existing LSAT Lab tab with `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: \\"iab\\" })`, using an ID from that inventory. A specifically mentioned tab instead uses `cua.getTab({ mention: completeMentionUrl })` as the initial call. Never invent a browser ID, tab ID, navigation method, locator API, or page-text reader. To create a missing tab, the docume…8667 tokens truncated… plugin-creator\\r\\ndescription: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Plugin Creator\\r\\n\\r\\n## Quick Start\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Run the scaffold script:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Plugin names are normalized to lower-case hyphen-case and must be <= 64 chars.\\r\\n# The generated folder and plugin.json name are always the same.\\r\\n# Run from the skill root (the directory containing this `SKILL.md`).\\r\\n# By default creates in `~/plugins/<plugin-name>`.\\r\\npython3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py <plugin-name>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n2. Edit `<plugin-path>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` when the request gives specific metadata.\\r\\n   The scaffold starts with valid defaults and must not contain `[TODO: ...]` placeholders.\\r\\n\\r\\n3. Generate or update the personal marketplace entry when the plugin should appear in Codex UI ordering:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Personal marketplace entries default to `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`.\\r\\npython3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py my-plugin --with-marketplace\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nOnly specify `--marketplace-name <name>` when the default `personal` marketplace name is already\\r\\ntaken or installed and you need to seed a different new marketplace file:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py my-plugin \\\\\\r\\n  --with-marketplace \\\\\\r\\n  --marketplace-name team-local\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nOnly use a repo/team marketplace when the user specifically asks for that destination:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py my-plugin \\\\\\r\\n  --path <repo-root>/plugins \\\\\\r\\n  --marketplace-path <repo-root>/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json \\\\\\r\\n  --with-marketplace\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the user specifies a marketplace path, make sure that marketplace is actually installed before\\r\\ntelling the user to reinstall from it. The default personal marketplace file at\\r\\n`~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is discovered implicitly, but other marketplace paths are not.\\r\\nOn Windows, use the equivalent path under the user profile.\\r\\n\\r\\n4. Generate/adjust optional companion folders as needed:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython3 scripts/create_basic_plugin.py my-plugin \\\\\\r\\n  --path <parent-plugin-directory> \\\\\\r\\n  --marketplace-path <marketplace-json-path> \\\\\\r\\n  --with-skills --with-hooks --with-scripts --with-assets --with-mcp --with-apps --with-marketplace\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n`<parent-plugin-directory>` is the directory where the plugin folder `<plugin-name>` will be\\r\\ncreated (for example `~/plugins`).\\r\\n\\r\\n5. Before handing back a generated plugin, run:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython3 scripts/validate_plugin.py <plugin-path>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nFor updates to an existing local plugin during development, keep the scaffold flow as-is and use the\\r\\nreference instead of hand-editing marketplace files:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython3 scripts/update_plugin_cachebuster.py <plugin-path>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nPrefer the helper default cachebuster unless the user explicitly asks for a specific override.\\r\\nSee `references/installing-and-updating.md` for the expected cachebuster and reinstall flow while iterating on an existing local plugin.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What this skill creates\\r\\n\\r\\n- Default marketplace-backed scaffolds use the personal marketplace file at\\r\\n  `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, with plugins generally being stored in\\r\\n  `~/plugins/<plugin-name>/`.\\r\\n- Creates plugin root at `/<parent-plugin-directory>/<plugin-name>/`.\\r\\n- Always creates `/<parent-plugin-directory>/<plugin-name>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`.\\r\\n- Fills the manifest with the validated schema shape that the ingestion path accepts.\\r\\n- Creates or updates `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` when `--with-marketplace` is set.\\r\\n  - If the marketplace file does not exist yet, seed a personal marketplace root before adding the first plugin entry.\\r\\n- `<plugin-name>` is normalized using skill-creator naming rules:\\r\\n  - `My Plugin` → `my-plugin`\\r\\n  - `My--Plugin` → `my-plugin`\\r\\n  - underscores, spaces, and punctuation are converted to `-`\\r\\n  - result is lower-case hyphen-delimited with consecutive hyphens collapsed\\r\\n- Supports optional creation of:\\r\\n  - `skills/`\\r\\n  - `hooks/`\\r\\n  - `scripts/`\\r\\n  - `assets/`\\r\\n  - `.mcp.json`\\r\\n  - `.app.json`\\r\\n\\r\\n## Marketplace workflow\\r\\n\\r\\n- Personal-marketplace creation defaults to `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. Here,\\r\\n  \\"personal marketplace\\" means the marketplace whose file is at that path.\\r\\n- Repo/team marketplace creation is opt-in through both `--path` and `--marketplace-path`, only\\r\\n  when the user specifically requests it.\\r\\n- `--marketplace-name` is an exception path. Use it only when the default `personal` marketplace\\r\\n  name is already taken and you need to seed a different new marketplace file.\\r\\n- Do not use `--marketplace-name` to rename an existing marketplace file in place. If the file\\r\\n  already exists, its top-level `name` must already match.\\r\\n- If the user specifies a different marketplace path, treat that marketplace as needing explicit installation via `codex plugin marketplace add`.\\r\\n- Prefer `scripts/read_marketplace_name.py` when you need the marketplace name from any\\r\\n  `marketplace.json` file. With no argument it reads the default personal marketplace; with an\\r\\n  explicit path it works for repo/team marketplaces too.\\r\\n- In either location, the generated source path remains `./plugins/<plugin-name>`.\\r\\n- Marketplace root metadata supports top-level `name` plus optional `interface.displayName`.\\r\\n- Treat plugin order in `plugins[]` as render order in Codex. Append new entries unless a user explicitly asks to reorder the list.\\r\\n- `displayName` belongs inside the marketplace `interface` object, not individual `plugins[]` entries.\\r\\n- Each generated marketplace entry must include all of:\\r\\n  - `policy.installation`\\r\\n  - `policy.authentication`\\r\\n  - `category`\\r\\n- Default new entries to:\\r\\n  - `policy.installation: \\"AVAILABLE\\"`\\r\\n  - `policy.authentication: \\"ON_INSTALL\\"`\\r\\n- Override defaults only when the user explicitly specifies another allowed value.\\r\\n- Allowed `policy.installation` values:\\r\\n  - `NOT_AVAILABLE`\\r\\n  - `AVAILABLE`\\r\\n  - `INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT`\\r\\n- Allowed `policy.authentication` values:\\r\\n  - `ON_INSTALL`\\r\\n  - `ON_USE`\\r\\n- Treat `policy.products` as an override. Omit it unless the user explicitly requests product gating.\\r\\n- The generated plugin entry shape is:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\"name\\": \\"plugin-name\\",\\r\\n  \\"source\\": {\\r\\n    \\"source\\": \\"local\\",\\r\\n    \\"path\\": \\"./plugins/plugin-name\\"\\r\\n  },\\r\\n  \\"policy\\": {\\r\\n    \\"installation\\": \\"AVAILABLE\\",\\r\\n    \\"authentication\\": \\"ON_INSTALL\\"\\r\\n  },\\r\\n  \\"category\\": \\"Productivity\\"\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use `--force` only when intentionally replacing an existing marketplace entry for the same plugin name.\\r\\n- If the target marketplace file does not exist yet, create it with top-level `\\"name\\"`, an `\\"interface\\"` object containing `\\"displayName\\"`, and a `plugins` array, then add the new entry.\\r\\n\\r\\n- For a brand-new marketplace file, the root object should look like:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\"name\\": \\"personal\\",\\r\\n  \\"interface\\": {\\r\\n    \\"displayName\\": \\"Personal\\"\\r\\n  },\\r\\n  \\"plugins\\": [\\r\\n    {\\r\\n      \\"name\\": \\"plugin-name\\",\\r\\n      \\"source\\": {\\r\\n        \\"source\\": \\"local\\",\\r\\n        \\"path\\": \\"./plugins/plugin-name\\"\\r\\n      },\\r\\n      \\"policy\\": {\\r\\n        \\"installation\\": \\"AVAILABLE\\",\\r\\n        \\"authentication\\": \\"ON_INSTALL\\"\\r\\n      },\\r\\n      \\"category\\": \\"Productivity\\"\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  ]\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required behavior\\r\\n\\r\\n- Outer folder name and `plugin.json` `\\"name\\"` are always the same normalized plugin name.\\r\\n- Do not remove required structure; Structure stability is the whole point.\\r\\n3. **Absolute paths always.** The next agent may have a different working directory, or be Codex.\\r\\n4. **If a plan file drove the session, name it first** in \\"Key files\\" so the next agent reads it before anything else.\\r\\n5. **No emojis, no hype, no \\"great job\\" summaries.** Terse and concrete — paths, commands, shell IDs, decisions. Tone of a seasoned engineer handing off at end-of-shift.\\r\\n6. **Background process IDs are critical.** If you started any `run_in_background` shells, their IDs must appear in \\"Running state\\" with the kill command — the next agent cannot find them otherwise.\\r\\n7. **Stamp verified state, and separate it from assumed state.** Read the current clock in the user\'s timezone and use the real time; on Windows use `Get-Date` with the applicable timezone conversion. Every claim about live systems (deploy status, DB contents, what was sent, what is published) is either something you actually checked this session — say how — or explicitly marked NOT re-verified. A handoff that presents stale belief as current state makes the next session re-derive everything, which is the exact cost this skill exists to remove.\\r\\n8. **Open questions are obligations, not notes.** Anything under OPEN must be resolved by the next session or re-asked to Joshua before it starts new work. Requirements have been silently re-typed across sessions, and a promised artifact once never arrived because nobody re-asked. If a question was open in the handoff you are picking up from, it is the first thing you raise.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anti-patterns — do not do these\\r\\n\\r\\n- Summarizing the last 3 turns and calling it a handoff.\\r\\n- Listing files by relative path.\\r\\n- Skipping \\"Running state\\" because \\"nothing is running\\" — write \\"none\\" instead.\\r\\n- Writing the summary to any file. This is chat-only by design.\\r\\n- Adding a \\"what went well / what went poorly\\" retrospective. This isn\'t a retro.\\r\\n- Recommending next steps beyond the single \\"Pick up here\\" line. The next agent decides; you just hand off.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\nFILE C:\\\\Users\\\\Joshu\\\\dev\\\\ai-os\\\\skills\\\\codex\\\\site-teardown\\\\SKILL.md\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: site-teardown\\r\\ndescription: \\"Reverse engineer any website into a complete build blueprint. Analyzes the HTML structure, fetches and extracts all animation/interaction code from the site\'s JavaScript, and pulls the complete design system from the CSS. Outputs a structured teardown document with tech stack, every visual effect and how it\'s implemented, design tokens, assets needed, and a section-by-section build plan. Use this skill whenever the user wants to analyze how a website was built, reverse engineer a site, clone or recreate a website, understand what tech stack or animations a site uses, do a site teardown, deconstruct a page, figure out how an effect works on a website, or says things like \'steal this website\', \'break down this site\', \'how did they build this\', \'website blueprint\', \'analyze this site for me\', or gives you a URL and asks you to figure out how it works. Also trigger when the user pastes raw HTML source code and asks what\'s going on or how to recreate it.\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Site Teardown\\r\\n\\r\\nReverse engineer any website into a complete build blueprint — tech stack, every visual effect with implementation details, full design system, and a section-by-section build plan. The output should be thorough enough that someone could hand it to a fresh agent session and build a clone without ever visiting the original site.\\r\\n\\r\\n## When This Skill Activates\\r\\n\\r\\n**Activate when the user wants to:**\\r\\n- Analyze how a website was built\\r\\n- Reverse engineer or deconstruct a site\\r\\n- Clone or recreate a website\'s design and animations\\r\\n- Understand what tech stack, libraries, or animation techniques a site uses\\r\\n- Get a build blueprint for a website they want to recreate\\r\\n- Understand how a specific effect on a website works (and the site hasn\'t been analyzed yet)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Example triggers:**\\r\\n- \\"Tear down this site: https://example.com\\"\\r\\n- \\"How did they build this website?\\"\\r\\n- \\"Analyze this site for me\\"\\r\\n- \\"Reverse engineer this page\\"\\r\\n- \\"I want to steal this website\'s design\\"\\r\\n- \\"Clone this site analysis\\"\\r\\n- \\"Website blueprint for [URL]\\"\\r\\n- \\"Break down this page\\"\\r\\n- \\"Deconstruct this site\\"\\r\\n- `/site-teardown`\\r\\n- `/site-teardown [URL]`\\r\\n- User pastes raw HTML and asks how to recreate it\\r\\n\\r\\n## Pipeline\\r\\n\\r\\n### Step 1 — Get the HTML\\r\\n\\r\\nThe HTML is the foundation. It tells you what\'s on the page — the elements, the classes, the structure, the image/video paths, the SVGs.\\r\\n\\r\\n**If the user pastes raw HTML source code:**\\r\\n- Use it directly. Pasted HTML is more complete than a WebFetch for large pages because WebFetch processes content through a sub-model that may summarize details.\\r\\n- Scan the HTML and extract key structural information:\\r\\n  - All section/component class names\\r\\n  - Image and video source paths\\r\\n  - SVG elements (logos, icons, decorative shapes)\\r\\n  - Form structures\\r\\n  - Navigation structure\\r\\n  - Meta tags (author, description, title)\\r\\n  - Any inline styles or inline scripts\\r\\n\\r\\n**If the user only provides a URL:**\\r\\n- Use WebFetch on the URL with this prompt: \\"Return the complete HTML structure of this page. Include all class names, element hierarchy, image/video src paths, SVG elements, meta tags, script src paths, stylesheet href paths, and any inline styles or scripts. Preserve the exact class names and data attributes. Do not summarize the structure — return as much detail as possible.\\"\\r\\n- Note to user: for the most complete analysis, they can paste the raw HTML (Ctrl+U → Ctrl+A → Ctrl+C on the page).\\r\\n\\r\\n### Step 2 — Find the JS and CSS File Paths\\r\\n\\r\\nFrom the HTML, locate the main application JavaScript and CSS files. These are what contain the actual behavior and styling.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Look for:**\\r\\n```html\\r\\n<!-- CSS - usually in <head> -->\\r\\n<link rel=\\"stylesheet\\" href=\\"/path/to/main.css\\">\\r\\n\\r\\n<!-- JS - usually before </body> -->\\r\\n<script src=\\"/path/to/main.js\\"></script>\\r\\n<script type=\\"module\\" src=\\"/dist/assets/app.js\\"></script>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Filter out third-party scripts** — skip these, they\'re not the site\'s custom code:\\r\\n- Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics, gtag\\r\\n- Cookie consent (iubenda, OneTrust, CookieBot)\\r\\n- reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha\\r\\n- CDN-hosted libraries (cdnjs, unpkg, jsdelivr) — note what libraries they use but don\'t fetch them\\r\\n- Social media widgets, chat widgets\\r\\n- WordPress core scripts (`/wp-includes/js/`)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Keep the main application files** — these are what you want:\\r\\n- Files from `/dist/`, `/build/`, `/assets/`, `/static/`\\r\\n- Files with names like `main.js`, `app.js`, `bundle.js`, `index.js`\\r\\n- Same pattern for CSS: `main.css`, `app.css`, `style.css`, `styles.css`\\r\\n- Modulepreload hints also point to important files: `<link rel=\\"modulepreload\\" href=\\"...\\">`\\r\\n\\r\\nConstruct the full URLs by combining the site\'s domain with the file paths.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Step 3 — Fetch the JavaScript\\r\\n\\r\\nUse WebFetch on the main JS file. The goal is to extract every interaction, animation, and behavior on the site.\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild the prompt dynamically using class names found in the HTML. Start with this base prompt and append the site-specific class names:\\r\\n\\r\\n**Base prompt:**\\r\\n```\\r\\nExtract ALL animation code, event listeners, scroll effects, mouse interactions,\\r\\nclick handlers, and GSAP/animation library usage from this JavaScript file.\\r\\n\\r\\nInclude:\\r\\n- Every function that manipulates the DOM, changes styles, or responds to user input\\r\\n- All ScrollTrigger/scroll-based animation configurations\\r\\n- All timeline definitions and animation sequences\\r\\n- All mousemove/mouseenter/mouseleave/click/touch handlers\\r\\n- All class toggling and DOM manipulation\\r\\n- All IntersectionObserver usage\\r\\n- All CSS custom property manipulation\\r\\n- All Lenis/locomotive/smooth scroll configurations\\r\\n- All Barba.js/Swup/page transition code\\r\\n- All slider/carousel/draggable configurations\\r\\n- All parallax implementations\\r\\n- All image sequence/frame animation logic\\r\\n- All cursor/pointer customization\\r\\n- All preloader/loading animations\\r\\n- All lazy loading logic\\r\\n- All form interaction handlers\\r\\n- All accordion/toggle/menu animations\\r\\n- Custom easing functions and timing values\\r\\n\\r\\nAlso look for any code targeting these class names from the HTML:\\r\\n[INSERT COMMA-SEPARATED LIST OF KEY CLASS NAMES FROM THE HTML]\\r\\n\\r\\nReturn actual code snippets with context about what elements they target.\\r\\nDo not summarize — return as much raw code as possible.\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace the class name placeholder with real classes extracted from the HTML in Step 1. Focus on classes that suggest interactivity — things with words like: hero, animate, scroll, slide, reveal, split, parallax, hover, active, open, toggle, frame, moon, star, video, zoom, marquee, cursor, loader, transition, etc.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Step 4 — Fetch the CSS\\r\\n\\r\\nUse WebFetch on the main CSS file. The goal is to extract the complete design system.\\r\\n\\r\\nAgain, build the prompt dynamically using actual class names from the HTML:\\r\\n\\r\\n**Base prompt:**\\r\\n```\\r\\nExtract the COMPLETE design system from this CSS file:\\r\\n\\r\\nInclude:\\r\\n- Every color value (hex, rgb, hsl, CSS custom properties)\\r\\n- Every @font-face declaration with font-family names, src paths, weights, and styles\\r\\n- Every font-family assignment and which elements use them\\r\\n- Every @keyframes animation with full keyframe definitions\\r\\n- Every CSS custom property (--variable) definition and usage\\r\\n- Every media query breakpoint and what changes at each\\r\\n- All transform and transition properties\\r\\n- All position:fixed and position:sticky elements\\r\\n- All z-index values and stacking context\\r\\n- The spacing/sizing system (padding, margin, gap patterns)\\r\\n- Border-radius values used across the site\\r\\n- Box-shadow and text-shadow values\\r\\n- Gradient definitions\\r\\n- Mix-blend-mode and filter usage\\r\\n- The responsive typography system (font sizes at different breakpoints)\\r\\n- Any CSS animations or transitions on pseudo-elements (::before, ::after)\\r\\n- Grid and flexbox layout patterns for major sections\\r\\n- Any mask-image or clip-path usage\\r\\n- The noise/grain/texture overlay implementation if present\\r\\n\\r\\nAlso extract all CSS rules for classes containing these terms:\\r\\n[INSERT COMMA-SEPARATED LIST OF KEY CLASS NAME STEMS FROM THE HTML]\\r\\n\\r\\nReturn actual CSS rules and values. Do not summarize — return as much raw CSS as possible.\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace the class name placeholder with stems extracted from the HTML. For example, if the HTML has `.home-hero__moon-inner`, include `hero`, `moon`. If it has `.circle-slider__wheel`, include `circle`, `slider`, `wheel`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Step 5 — Assemble the Teardown Document\\r\\n\\r\\nCombine findings from all three sources (HTML, JS, CSS) into a structured markdown file.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Save to:** The user\'s working directory at `research/YYYY-MM-DD-{site-slug}-teardown.md`\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the working directory doesn\'t have a `research/` folder, save to the current directory instead.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Use this template:**\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\n# Site Teardown: {Site Name}\\r\\n\\r\\n**URL:** {url}\\r\\n**Built by:** {agency/developer if identifiable from meta tags or footer}\\r\\n**Platform:** {WordPress/Next.js/custom/etc — inferred from HTML structure}\\r\\n**Date analyzed:** {YYYY-MM-DD}\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tech Stack (Confirmed from Source)\\r\\n\\r\\n| Technology | Evidence | Purpose |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| {library} | {where you saw it — script tag, code reference, etc.} | {what it does on this site} |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Design System\\r\\n\\r\\n### Colors\\r\\n| Name/Usage | Value |\\r\\n|---|---|\\r\\n| {Primary background} | {#hex} |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Typography\\r\\n| Role | Font Family | Weight | Letter-spacing | Sizes |\\r\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\r\\n| {Headings} | {font name} | {weight} | {spacing} | {size range} |\\r\\n\\r\\nFont files: {list actual font file paths if found in @font-face}\\r\\n\\r\\n### Spacing System\\r\\n{Describe the spacing approach — CSS custom properties, fluid sizing with min()/clamp(), fixed values, etc.}\\r\\n\\r\\n### Responsive Approach\\r\\n{Media query strategy — breakpoints, orientation-based, container queries, etc.}\\r\\n\\r\\n## Effects Breakdown\\r\\n\\r\\n| Effect | Implementation | Complexity | Cloneable? |\\r\\n|---|---|---|---|\\r\\n| {effect name} | {how it works — 1-2 sentences} | {Low/Med/High} | {Yes/Partially/Hard} |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation Details\\r\\n\\r\\n### {Most Impressive Effect #1}\\r\\n```\\r\\n{Detailed explanation of how it works}\\r\\n{Code snippets from the JS/CSS fetch}\\r\\n{The key insight that makes it work}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### {Most Impressive Effect #2}\\r\\n```\\r\\n{Same structure}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n{Repeat for each major effect worth detailing}\\r\\n\\r\\n## Assets Needed to Recreate\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **{Asset type}** — {description, suggested source (Midjourney prompt, stock site, generate with code, etc.)}\\r\\n\\r\\n## Build Plan\\r\\n\\r\\n### Recommended Stack\\r\\n- {Framework}: {why}\\r\\n- {Styling}: {why}\\r\\n- {Animation library}: {why}\\r\\n- {Other packages}: {why}\\r\\n\\r\\n### NPM Packages\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nnpm install {package1} {package2} {package3}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Section-by-Section Build Order\\r\\n\\r\\n**Section 1: {name}**\\r\\n- {what it contains}\\r\\n- {key interactions/animations}\\r\\n- {implementation approach}\\r\\n\\r\\n**Section 2: {name}**\\r\\n- {same structure}\\r\\n\\r\\n{Continue for all sections}\\r\\n\\r\\n## Notes\\r\\n- {Any gotchas, premium plugins needed, licensing concerns}\\r\\n- {Things that can\'t be cloned easily and suggested alternatives}\\r\\n- {Performance considerations}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Filling the Template — Guidance\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen assembling the teardown, keep these principles in mind:\\r\\n\\r\\n**Be specific, not vague.** \\"GSAP ScrollTrigger with scrub:true pinned to .hero, scaling from 1 to 0.3\\" is useful. \\"Uses scroll animations\\" is not. The person reading this needs to build it without seeing the original site.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Include the \\"reveal\\" for each effect.** The most valuable part of a teardown is showing that an impressive-looking effect has a simple implementation. If the moon illumination is just 54 images swapped on mousemove, say that clearly. If the parallax is just `translateX(mouseX / 50)`, include that formula.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Distinguish confirmed vs inferred.** If you found the exact GSAP config in the JS, say \\"confirmed from source.\\" If you\'re inferring from HTML class names and general patterns, say \\"inferred\\" so the builder knows what\'s solid and what might need adjustment.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Group effects by section.** The effects table gives the overview, but the implementation details should follow the page flow top-to-bottom so the builder can work section by section.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Be practical about assets.** Don\'t just say \\"needs images.\\" Say how many, what kind, suggest Midjourney prompts or stock photo search terms, and note if any can be generated with code (SVGs, noise textures, gradients).\\r\\n\\r\\n## Common Patterns to Watch For\\r\\n\\r\\nThese are the most common \\"impressive-looking but simple\\" patterns found on award-winning sites:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Image sequences on scroll/mouse** — Preloaded frames, swap visibility based on input. Looks like video/3D, it\'s just images.\\r\\n- **SplitText character reveals** — GSAP SplitText wraps each character in a span, then staggers their opacity/transform.\\r\\n- **Parallax layers** — Multiple elements moving at different speeds on mousemove or scroll. Just different multipliers on transform.\\r\\n- **Scroll-scrubbed animations** — GSAP ScrollTrigger with `scrub: true`. Ties any animation to scroll position.\\r\\n- **CSS custom property animations** — JS updates a `--progress` variable, CSS uses `calc()` with it. Clean separation of behavior and style.\\r\\n- **Smooth scrolling** — Lenis or Locomotive Scroll wrapping the page. Just a library init.\\r\\n- **Page transitions** — Barba.js or Swup. Overlay fades in, content swaps, overlay fades out.\\r\\n- **Noise/grain overlay** — A fixed div with a noise texture image and `mix-blend-mode: overlay`.\\r\\n- **Custom cursors** — GSAP `quickSetter` tracking mouse position on a fixed element.\\r\\n- **Marquee text** — CSS or GSAP infinite horizontal translation loop.\\r\\n- **Magnetic buttons** — Element subtly follows cursor when hovering nearby. Just mousemove + transform on the button.\\r\\n- **Reveal on scroll** — IntersectionObserver or ScrollTrigger adding a class, CSS handles the transition.\\r\\n\\r\\n"}'}]
