keep the product and its edges unchanged; no text; no watermark\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Prompting best practices\\r\\n- Structure prompt as scene/backdrop -> subject -> details -> constraints.\\r\\n- Include intended use (ad, UI mock, infographic) to set the mode and polish level.\\r\\n- Use camera/composition language for photorealism.\\r\\n- Only use SVG/vector stand-ins when the user explicitly asked for vector output or a non-image placeholder.\\r\\n- Quote exact text and specify typography + placement.\\r\\n- For tricky words, spell them letter-by-letter and require verbatim rendering.\\r\\n- For multi-image inputs, reference images by index and describe how they should be used.\\r\\n- For edits, repeat invariants every iteration to reduce drift.\\r\\n- Iterate with single-change follow-ups.\\r\\n- If the prompt is generic, add only the extra detail that will materially help.\\r\\n- If the prompt is already detailed, normalize it instead of expanding it.\\r\\n- For CLI fallback only, see `references/cli.md` and `references/image-api.md` for model, `quality`, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, and output-path guidance.\\r\\n- For transparent images, use the built-in-first chroma-key workflow unless the request is complex enough to need true CLI transparency; Codex: OpenAI\'s coding agent for software development that can write, understand, review, and debug code.\\r\\n5. gpt-oss: Open-weight OpenAI reasoning models (gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b) released under the Apache 2.0 license.\\r\\n6. Realtime API: Build low-latency, multimodal experiences including natural speech-to-speech conversations.\\r\\n7. Agents SDK: A toolkit for building agentic apps where a model can use tools and context, hand off to other agents, stream partial results, and keep a full trace.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Codex self-knowledge\\r\\n\\r\\nUse this path for questions about Codex itself: configuring, extending, operating, troubleshooting, local state, product surfaces, or where Codex behavior should live. If the exact term remains material or likely current after that manual pass, use one narrow Docs MCP search/fetch before bounded uncertainty; otherwise, the source lookup for that terminology or mapping claim is complete.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the narrowest official next source only when the manual is unavailable, the helper fails, temp caching is not allowed, another material claim is missing or likely stale, or the user explicitly needs a page-specific citation. Those labels are not a reason to leave the public source route.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor support-style diagnostics, prefer a layer-by-layer answer from the manual over provider-specific web lookups: installed/enabled plugin, bundled app or connector authorization, MCP setup, workspace/admin policy, restart or new-thread expectations, then support or feedback if still unresolved.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the source route still does not establish a claim, return bounded uncertainty or route to support, an admin, or product feedback instead of widening the investigation.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor unresolved product terminology, answer from the manual plus the allowed official next source. If those sources do not establish the term, answer with bounded uncertainty from those sources.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Surface Map\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen Codex nouns or durable-instruction surfaces overlap, recommend the smallest surface that matches the scope:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Prompt or thread context -> one-off task constraints.\\r\\n- `AGENTS.md` -> durable repo conventions, commands, verification steps, and review expectations; closer nested files apply under their subtree.\\r\\n- Project `.codex/config.toml` -> trusted-repo Codex settings such as sandbox, MCP, hooks, model, or reasoning defaults.\\r\\n- Global config or global guidance -> personal defaults across repos.\\r\\n- Skill -> reusable task workflow with references or scripts.\\r\\n- Plugin -> installable bundle with skills plus commands, tools, MCP config, hooks, assets, apps, or marketplace metadata.\\r\\n- MCP server or app connector -> live external data/actions or authorized private app/workspace data. Use connectors for private Google Docs, Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Notion, and similar data instead of web search or model memory.\\r\\n- Automation -> scheduled checks, reminders, monitors, or follow-up work; use a thread heartbeat when continuity in an existing thread matters.\\r\\n- Hook -> lifecycle enforcement around tool calls, commands, or file edits.\\r\\n\\r\\nSplit mixed-scope requests instead of forcing one answer. Example: \\"always do X, but only for this PR\\" defaults to prompt/thread context for the current run; use `AGENTS.md` or project config only if it should persist, hooks only for mechanical enforcement, and automations only for scheduled or follow-up work.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse this quick product map when needed: CLI is terminal-first local repo work; IDE extension is editor-attached coding; Codex app is desktop planning, review, and interactive work; cloud/web is hosted parallel/offloaded work; Browser Use/in-app browser is Codex-controlled web testing; Chrome extension uses the user\'s Chrome profile; Computer Use controls desktop apps and OS UI. Keep `config.toml` defaults, `requirements.toml` constraints, and managed/admin policy separate.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Boundaries And Output\\r\\n\\r\\n- API key auth does not imply ChatGPT, cloud task, or connector access. For plugin/app/auth failures, check bundle availability, plugin installed/enabled state, connector/app authorization, MCP setup, restart/refresh expectations, workspace policy, and per-surface availability before answering.\\r\\n- Sandbox or network denials need scoped escalation with a clear justification. Destructive commands, writes outside the workspace, or broad access changes require explicit approval.\\r\\n- Memory can provide user preference or context, but explicit prompt instructions win and memory is not a source for current external facts.\\r\\n- For affirmative surface-selection answers, use this shape: recommendation, why, what to avoid, and the manual/source evidence used.\\r\\n- When page-specific Codex citations are actually needed, these anchors often fit: `concepts/customization#agents-guidance` for `AGENTS.md`, `concepts/customization#skills` for skills, `plugins/build#plugin-structure` for plugins, `concepts/customization#mcp` for MCP, `config-advanced#hooks` for hooks, `app/automations#thread-automations` for thread automations, and `config-reference#configtoml` for config.\\r\\n\\r\\n## If MCP server is missing\\r\\n\\r\\nIf MCP tools fail or no OpenAI docs resources are available:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Run the install command yourself: `codex mcp add openaiDeveloperDocs --url https://developers.openai.com/mcp`\\r\\n2. If it fails due to permissions/sandboxing, immediately retry the same command with escalated permissions and include a 1-sentence justification for approval.\\r\\n3. Ask the user to run the install command only if the escalated attempt fails.\\r\\n4. Ask the user to restart Codex.\\r\\n5. Re-run the doc search/fetch after restart.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Workflow\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Clarify whether the request is general docs lookup, model selection, a model-string upgrade, prompt-upgrade guidance, or broader API/provider migration.\\r\\n2. For Codex self-knowledge requests, follow the Codex self-knowledge source procedure above.\\r\\n3. For model-selection or upgrade requests, prefer current remote docs over bundled references when the user asks for latest/current/default guidance.\\r\\n   - Fetch `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.md`.\\r\\n   - Find the latest model ID and explicit migration or prompt-guidance links.\\r\\n   - Prefer explicit links from the latest-model page over derived URLs.\\r\\n   - For explicit named-model requests, preserve the requested model target. Mention newer remote guidance only as optional.\\r\\n   - For dynamic latest/current/default upgrades, run `node scripts/resolve-latest-model-info.js`, then fetch both returned guide URLs directly when possible.\\r\\n   - If direct guide fetch fails, use the developer-docs MCP tools or official OpenAI-domain search to find the same guide content.\\r\\n   - If remote docs are unavailable, use bundled fallback references and say that fallback guidance was used.\\r\\n4. For model upgrades, keep changes narrow: update active OpenAI API model defaults and directly related prompts only when safe.\\r\\n5. Leave historical docs, examples, eval baselines, fixtures, provider comparisons, provider registries, pricing tables, alias defaults, low-cost fallback paths, and ambiguous older model usage unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to upgrade them.\\r\\n6. Keep SDK, tooling, IDE, plugin, shell, auth, and provider-environment migrations out of a model-and-prompt upgrade unless the user explicitly asks for them.\\r\\n7. If an upgrade needs API-surface changes, schema rewiring, tool-handler changes, or implementation work beyond a literal model-string replacement and prompt edits, report it as blocked or confirmation-needed.\\r\\n8. For general docs lookup, start with a compact, title-like search query of 2-6 essential terms. Do not turn the full user question into a keyword list. Fetch the best page and exact section needed, and answer with concise citations.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Reference map\\r\\n\\r\\nRead only what you need:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.md` -> current model-selection and \\"best/latest/current model\\" questions.\\r\\n- `scripts/fetch-codex-manual.mjs` -> current Codex manual fetch, verification, local temp cache, and outline generation.\\r\\n- `https://developers.openai.com/codex/codex-manual.md` -> current Codex self-knowledge synthesis, including setup, customization, skills, plugins, MCP, hooks, `AGENTS.md`, automations, and surface behavior; normally access it through the helper path and targeted file reads when temp caching is available.\\r\\n- `references/latest-model.md` -> bundled fallback for model-selection and \\"best/latest/current model\\" questions.\\r\\n- `references/upgrade-guide.md` -> bundled fallback for model upgrade and upgrade-planning requests.\\r\\n- `references/prompting-guide.md` -> bundled fallback for prompt rewrites and prompt-behavior upgrades.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Quality rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- Treat OpenAI docs as the source of truth; avoid speculation.\\r\\n- For Codex self-knowledge, follow the source route above instead of relying on remembered behavior.\\r\\n- Keep migration changes narrow and behavior-preserving.\\r\\n- Prefer prompt-only upgrades when possible.\\r\\n- Avoid inventing pricing, availability, parameters, API changes, or breaking changes.\\r\\n- Keep quotes short and within policy limits; prefer paraphrase with citations.\\r\\n- If multiple pages differ, call out the difference and cite both.\\r\\n- If official docs and verified callable current-session behavior disagree, state the conflict before making broad claims or edits.\\r\\n- If docs do not cover the user’s need, say so and offer next steps.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tooling notes\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use MCP doc tools before web search for OpenAI-related markdown docs. The Codex manual flow is the exception: follow the Codex self-knowledge source procedure for broad Codex synthesis.\\r\\n- If the MCP server is installed but returns no meaningful results, then use web search as a fallback.\\r\\n- When falling back to web search, restrict to official OpenAI domains (developers.openai.com, platform.openai.com) and cite sources.\\r\\n"}'}]

Assign complete interactive Classroom lessons directly through the local lsat-u-lessons MCP server, verify the saved content and student visibility headlessly, and log the assignment. Use the Node CLI for other supported actions.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nFor drills, messages, student data, access, signups, due dates, unassign, and unsend, use `assign-lsatu-work`. On Windows, invoke its Node entry point directly instead of relying on Bash being on PATH.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n# LSAT U Platform Actions\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua\'s workplace is this brain workspace. LSAT U operations should run headlessly when a supported tool exists. The browser is for checking what a person sees.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Mechanism\\r\\n\\r\\nFor an interactive HTML lesson, call the `lsat-u-lessons` MCP tool `publish_interactive_lesson` with the student\'s exact email, absolute HTML path, and title. The local stdio server is `system/scripts/lsatu-lesson-mcp.mjs`; Codex registration is `lsat-u-lessons`. It calls `system/scripts/lsatu-admin.mjs post-lesson`, which authenticates with the existing admin credentials, posts through `mcp_post_classroom_note`, verifies the saved HTML exactly and student visibility, and then archives only earlier versions with the same lesson marker. A repeat of the current version returns the same item without another notification. Use `dry_run: true` when the student or replacement is uncertain; otherwise publish in one call. MCP tools newly registered during a session may only appear in a new Codex session; the direct Node command is the immediate fallback.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe HTML must be a complete document inside AI OS, under 500 KB, with `<meta name=\\"lsatu-interactive-lesson\\" content=\\"unique-lesson-id\\">`. Reuse the same lesson ID for revisions of that lesson; use a different ID for a different lesson. Inline the CSS, JavaScript, fonts, and visual assets. Preflight rejects nonembedded resources; do not bypass it or paste HTML into an ordinary sanitized note. The already-live Classroom renderer loads marked HTML in a sandboxed iframe with scripts and forms enabled. **Daily lesson posting is a content operation and never requires Lovable.** Only an actual app renderer change follows the separate app deployment rules.\\r\\n\\r\\nRoutine verification is headless: the publisher reads the new item back, compares its HTML byte for byte, checks that it is visible to the intended student, and confirms one active version. The result includes its route and SHA-256. Use Codex\'s in-app browser only when a visual or interaction defect is suspected or the page design or renderer changed. A teacher login cannot open another student\'s `/classroom/item/<id>` route directly. Do not claim a student-session visual check unless one was actually performed.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe student opens the full lesson from Classroom **Notes and recaps**, the in-app notification, or its Inbox link. Classroom Home may show a recent note as a “Read” row, but it has a four-row limit shared with urgent work, so do not promise that every assigned note stays on Home. This does not affect the note\'s visibility in Notes and recaps or its direct item route.\\r\\n\\r\\n## UI fallback routing\\r\\n\\r\\nThe current student verification route is `/teacher/students/<student-id>/notes`. Its “Posted to their Classroom” section shows active notes and labels archived notes as hidden from the student. Use the browser\'s normal controls for any unsupported action, then verify the saved state through a fresh read. In Codex, use the in-app browser, not Chrome. Do not rely on old `/teacher?ws=` routes or old browser-tool names.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Order of operations (every action)\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Identify the student** exactly (roster names include email; ambiguity → one\\r\\n   concise clarifying question). Check `students/<name>/` for context and\\r\\n   `assignment-log.md` to avoid repeats.\\r\\n2. **Do the action** through MCP or the headless Node CLI when supported. Use the UI fallback only for unsupported actions.\\r\\n3. **Verify it landed**: use the publisher\'s read-after-write result to confirm exact HTML, student visibility, and one active copy of this lesson ID. It archives earlier versions of that ID and leaves unrelated same-title notes alone. Check notifications where available. If verification fails, inspect current items before retrying; never blindly post twice.\\r\\n4. **Log it**: append to `students/<name>/assignment-log.md` (create if missing) with\\r\\n   date, action, item, and evidence; drill verifications also go to\\r\\n   `wiki/guided-drill-verification-log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Guardrails\\r\\n\\r\\n- Every action here hits **real students on prod**. Anything a student will see\\r\\n  (message text, homework instructions, note bodies) is written in Joshua\'s voice —\\r\\n  route through `wiki/teaching-voice.md`.\\r\\n- If Joshua\'s request fully specifies the action (\\"assign Lydia the conditional\\r\\n  drill\\"), execute without re-asking. If content is open-ended (a message body he\\r\\n  hasn\'t dictated), draft it and show him before sending.\\r\\n- Fail closed: if verification is ambiguous, say exactly what was and wasn\'t\\r\\n  confirmed. Never report an action complete on the strength of a click alone.\\r\\n- No student-facing action as a side effect of a different request.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Paid session credits\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `node system/scripts/lsatu-admin.mjs passes <exact-email>` for balances and `pass-detail` for evidence. An exhausted pass can be replaced with `pass-create <exact-email> --credits N --minutes 70`; dry-run first, then verify through a fresh read. Preserve exhausted passes.\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore manually restoring a Stripe package, inspect its `stripe_payments` row and the webhook delivery response. The 2026-09-27 policy returned `grant: awaiting_teacher` for intentional teacher approval. On 2026-10-02, Joshua approved and deployed automatic crediting for new validated, confidently matched package Checkouts, including delayed successes. Existing rows default `auto_grant_eligible=false`; historical, dismissed, and granted payments are not automatically recredited. Unmatched payments stay in review. Verify the live row and deployment before diagnosing a bug; an empty `booking_commerce_events` read is not proof of no payment. Evidence: `research/2026-10-02-celia-payment-crediting.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\nAssociate any manual restoration with its exact Stripe payment/event in the booking pass notes. Reconcile the pending teacher grant prompt without adding more credits, using the supported payment-ledger operation after checking its semantics. Do not replay the webhook or invoke `admin_grant_stripe_payment` after manual crediting; either can duplicate sessions. A dismissed payment is not marked granted, and future reconciliation must skip it or explicitly honor the manual fulfillment.\\r\\n"}'}]

Activate for \\"session write up\\", \\"session write-up\\", \\"make a post-session recap\\", \\"write up the session\\", \\"recap my last session\\", \\"make session notes\\", \\"[student] session\\", or similar requests to turn a completed tutoring session into a lesson. In an established tutoring-session context, \\"write up\\", \\"recap\\", and \\"make notes\\" also activate it. Own transcript intake, student record, teaching note, interactive preview, verification, and filing. Explicit transcript lookup or inspection stays narrow; posting and assignment require authorization.\\n---\\n\\n# Post Session Recap\\n\\n## When to activate\\n\\nRecognize the intent to turn an LSAT tutoring session into a finished post-session lesson. The examples below are natural language, not required commands. Accept capitalization, punctuation, hyphenation, and ordinary wording variations. Do not require the exact skill name or a second instruction to create the lesson after intake.\\n\\n**Clear activation phrases:**\\n\\n- \\"Session write up\\" or \\"session write-up.\\"\\n- \\"Make a post-session recap for the session\\" or \\"create a post session recap.\\"\\n- \\"Write up the session,\\" \\"write up my last session,\\" or \\"write up the session I just finished.\\"\\n- \\"Recap the session,\\" \\"recap my last session,\\" or \\"make a recap of today\'s tutoring session.\\"\\n- \\"Make session notes,\\" \\"prepare the post-session notes,\\" or \\"turn the session into a lesson.\\"\\n- \\"[Student] session,\\" \\"write up [student]\'s session,\\" or \\"make [student]\'s session recap.\\"\\n- \\"Write up this transcript,\\" \\"make a lesson from this session transcript,\\" or an attached tutoring transcript with a request for notes or a recap.\\n- \\"Make a review note for the student from our session\\" or \\"write up what the student should review after the session.\\"\\n\\n**Short requests use context:** \\"write up,\\" \\"recap,\\" \\"make notes,\\" \\"today\'s session,\\" \\"the last session,\\" and \\"the current session\\" activate the full workflow when the conversation clearly refers to an LSAT tutoring session. In an unrelated or empty context, bare \\"write up,\\" \\"recap,\\" or \\"notes\\" is not enough to assume a tutoring request. Ask one short clarification if its subject cannot be established. A named student\'s session is enough to activate the full workflow, not merely intake.\\n\\n**Resolve the session without requiring a magic phrase:** Honor an explicit student, date, or supplied transcript first. Otherwise use the session already identified in this conversation. If no session is identified, an explicit session write-up or post-session recap request refers to the most recent completed tutoring session; verify it through Calendar and the intake procedure, using America/Toronto for relative dates. \\"[Student] session\\" without a date refers to that student\'s most recent completed tutoring session. Confirm student and absolute date from the evidence before writing. Ask only when multiple plausible sessions remain or the evidence cannot establish the intended session. Retrieve or inspect the source and answer the request. Mentioning a session in scheduling, payment, cancellation, or consultation correspondence does not activate this skill. The student should be able to return days later, understand the concept without the original question, test the method, and see why each answer works. The [lesson quality bar](references/lesson-quality-bar.md) describes the finished experience. Meet its teaching standard every time; vary the visual treatment to fit the subject. Follow the [transcript intake and primary-record procedure](references/transcript-intake-and-record.md), then create the student-facing lesson and preview. MAX_ROUNDS=<n>.\\n+```\\n+\\n+---\\n+\\n+## ACT 2 — REVIEW (Claude ↔ Codex)\\n+\\n+Hand the locked plan to Codex for adversarial review. Mechanics verified end-to-end (2026-06-04).\\n+\\n+### Prerequisites\\n+- `codex --version` ≥ 0.130 (older CLIs error on the default `gpt-5.5` model).\\n+- Codex authenticated (`codex login`; ChatGPT account fine). If the user objects, stop before burning a round.\\n+\\n+### Tunables (args, else default)\\n+| Var | Default | Meaning |\\n+|-----|---------|---------|\\n+| `MAX_ROUNDS` | `5` | Hard cap. Loop ALWAYS terminates here. |\\n+| `PLAN_FILE` | `PLAN.md` | The plan from Act 1. |\\n+| `LOG_FILE` | `PLAN-REVIEW-LOG.md` | Append-only argument transcript. |\\n+\\n+Invoked with e.g. `rounds=3` → use it. Echo resolved values first.\\n+\\n+### Review prompt (each round)\\n+> You are an adversarial reviewer for an implementation plan. Be skeptical and specific — your job is to find what breaks, not to be agreeable. Read the plan at `PLAN.md` (and `CONTEXT.md`/ADRs for the domain language) and any repo files you need (you are read-only). Identify concrete flaws: security holes, race conditions, missing edge cases, schema conflicts, domain-language mismatches, wrong assumptions, observability gaps, simpler alternatives. For each, give a one-line fix. Do NOT modify any files. End with EXACTLY one line: `VERDICT: APPROVED` or `VERDICT: REVISE`.\\n+\\n+### Round 1 — fresh session (capture `thread_id`)\\n+```bash\\n+codex exec -s read-only --json -o /tmp/codex-verdict.txt \\"$(cat REVIEW_PROMPT)\\" \\\\\\n+  < /dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep \'\\"type\\":\\"thread.started\\"\'\\n+```\\n+Parse `thread_id` from the `thread.started` line. Critique in `/tmp/codex-verdict.txt`. No verdict file + no `thread.started` = failed run (auth/model) → stop, tell the user. `2>/dev/null` hides cosmetic MCP/auth noise. **`< /dev/null` is mandatory:** `codex exec` reads stdin *in addition to* the prompt arg, so under a non-interactive driver (Claude Code\'s Bash tool, CI, any non-TTY pipeline) it blocks forever waiting on stdin EOF — a silent ~0% CPU hang. Re-review PLAN.md — check prior findings + flag anything new. End with VERDICT: APPROVED or VERDICT: REVISE.\\" \\\\\\n+  < /dev/null 2>/dev/null >/dev/null\\n+```\\n+The `< /dev/null` redirect is required on the resume call too — same non-interactive stdin hang as Round 1.\\n+\\n+**Timeout guard (both rounds):** run every `codex exec` / `codex exec resume` with a 10-minute ceiling so any future stall fails loud instead of hanging silently. Read verdict file; append `## Round <n> — Codex` + critique to `LOG_FILE`.\\n+2. Last line verdict: `APPROVED` → Resolution (converged); `REVISE` → Claude decides what\'s worth acting on (final arbiter), revise `PLAN_FILE`, append `### Claude\'s response` (what changed/rejected + why), increment.\\n+3. round > `MAX_ROUNDS` → Resolution (deadlock).\\n+\\n+### Resolution (you sign off)\\n+- **APPROVED:** present final plan + 3-bullet summary of what the two acts improved + round count. Never writes.\\n+- Loop ALWAYS terminates at `MAX_ROUNDS`. Claude is final arbiter on REVISE (reject with logged reason). [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"6493a1","wall_time_seconds":1.4814232,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":956,"output":"---\\r\\nname: skill-lint\\r\\ndescription: Use when a repo skill fails, produces errors, gives wrong instructions, or references stale information. Also use when a command from a skill returns \\"not found\\" or \\"unknown flag\\", when a skill references a file path that doesn\'t exist, when a skill\'s behavior doesn\'t match the codebase, or to list available skills, manage local overrides, check staleness, or optimize token usage and quality.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Skill Doctor\\r\\n\\r\\nDiagnose issues with repository skills, manage local overrides, and optimize skill quality.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Scope:** Skills in the current repository\'s `.claude/skills/` directory only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Routing\\r\\n\\r\\nParse `$ARGUMENTS`:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Pattern | Mode |\\r\\n|---------|------|\\r\\n| `list` | **list** (all repo skills) |\\r\\n| `info <skill>` | **list** (detail for one skill) |\\r\\n| `feedback [skill] \\"<message>\\"` | **feedback** (quick note) |\\r\\n| (empty) or `<skill-name>` | **diagnose** |\\r\\n| `--optimize <skill>` | **optimize** |\\r\\n| `--manage [skill]` | **manage** (status) |\\r\\n| `clone/diff/sync/revert <skill>` | **manage** (lifecycle) |\\r\\n| `report/gist/pr <skill>` | **deliver** |\\r\\n| `resolve <skill>` | **resolve** |\\r\\n\\r\\nUnrecognized input: show this table and ask to rephrase. Then **read `./reference.md`** for detailed procedures.\\r\\n\\r\\n## List\\r\\n\\r\\nDynamically discovers repo skills by reading `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`. Shows name, description, invocation, and override status. `info <skill>` reads the full SKILL.md to provide detailed usage guidance. All information comes from the skill files themselves — nothing is hardcoded. See reference.md for details.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Feedback\\r\\n\\r\\nLightweight path for quick notes. No investigation or quality gate — just scrub, preview, confirm, post. If skill name is omitted, ask which skill (or use the most recently invoked skill if known from conversation context). See reference.md for details.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Manage\\r\\n\\r\\nLifecycle: clone -> edit -> diff -> sync/revert -> pr/gist. Local overrides live at `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` with `.skill-origin.json` tracking.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Diagnose\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Identify** skill, validate it exists\\r\\n2. **Classify**: `invalid_command` | `wrong_assumption` | `stale_info` | `other`\\r\\n3. **Investigate** -- reproduce, root cause, determine fix, check related issues. Quality gate: confirmed problem + root cause + suggested fix\\r\\n4. **Duplicate check** in Discussion thread. Match found: upvote, add context, or report anyway\\r\\n5. **Route**: local override -> fix inline, stop. Repo -> offer clone-and-fix or report-only\\r\\n6. **Scrub** PII, **review** with developer, **deliver** to GitHub Discussion + Slack\\r\\n\\r\\n## Optimize\\r\\n\\r\\nChecks frontmatter, token efficiency (<500 words), structure quality, and staleness (file paths, commands, flags). Scored report with fixes. Local overrides fixed directly; repo versions cloned first.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Deliver & Resolve\\r\\n\\r\\n**Deliver**: GitHub Discussion (primary, one thread per skill) + Slack `#log-skill-feedback` (optional notification). Check prerequisites first (gh auth, repo access). See reference.md.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Resolve**: After fix PR merges, mark Discussion reports resolved, post Slack summary, offer to lock thread.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Common Mistakes\\r\\n\\r\\nSee reference.md for the full table. Key rules:\\r\\n- Never send reports without root cause + suggested fix\\r\\n- Always check Discussion thread for duplicates before reporting\\r\\n- Always run `gh auth status` before any delivery action\\r\\n- `revert` always shows diff and requires name confirmation\\r\\n\\r\\n## Override Warning\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen ANY skill is invoked and `~/.claude/skills/<name>/.skill-origin.json` exists, output before skill content:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nSKILL OVERRIDE ACTIVE: <name>\\r\\n  Using: ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ (local)\\r\\n  Instead of: .claude/skills/<name>/ (repo)\\r\\n  Cloned from: <sha> | Repo is N commits ahead\\r\\n  Run /skill-doctor --manage <name> for options\\r\\n```\\r\\n"}'}]

Most paths run along one **main flow**, and two **on-ramps** merge onto it. Everything else is standalone, or a vocabulary layer that runs underneath.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The main flow: idea → ship\\r\\n\\r\\nThe route most work travels. You have an idea and want it built.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **`/grill-with-docs`** sharpens the idea by interview. Start here whenever you are **working in a working directory**: it\'s stateful, retaining what it learns in `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs. (No working directory? Use `/grill-me` instead, covered under Standalone. Both run the same `/grilling` primitive; `grill-with-docs` is the one that leaves a paper trail, which makes it the better of the two whenever a repo is there to leave it in.)\\r\\n2. **Branch: can you settle every question in conversation?** If a question needs a runnable answer (state, business logic, a UI you have to see), detour through a prototype, bridged by **`/handoff`** in both directions (a prototype lives in its own directory, which is exactly what `/handoff` is for; see Phase boundaries):\\r\\n   - **`/handoff`** out, then open a fresh session against that file,\\r\\n   - **`/prototype`** to answer the question with throwaway code,\\r\\n   - **`/handoff`** back what you learned, and reference it from the original idea thread.\\r\\n3. **Branch: is this a multi-session build?**\\r\\n   - **Yes** → **`/to-spec`** (turn the thread into a spec), then **`/to-tickets`** to split it into tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its **blocking edges**. Then work the tickets one of two ways:\\r\\n     - **`/implement`** per ticket, **`/clear`ing context between each one**. On a local tracker that\'s one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature>/issues/`, worked blockers-first by hand; on a real tracker the edges become native blocking links, so any ticket whose blockers are done can be grabbed. Each ticket is self-contained, so the last one\'s context is disposable.\\r\\n     - **`/implement-spec`** for the whole spec in one run. It reads the tickets as a **task graph**, runs implementer subagents across the ready **frontier** in parallel, and lands everything on one **integration branch**. Reach for it when you\'d rather orchestrate the build than drive each ticket yourself.\\r\\n   - **No** → **`/implement`** right here, in the same context window.\\r\\n\\r\\n   Either way, the code gets built by driving **`/tdd`** (one red-green slice at a time) and closes out with **`/code-review`**, a two-axis review (Standards + Spec) of the diff. `/implement` runs both per ticket; `/implement-spec`\'s implementers each drive `/tdd`, and it runs one `/code-review` over the integration branch. Reach for **`/tdd`** on its own when you just want to build a concrete behaviour test-first without a full spec, and **`/code-review`** on its own whenever you want to review a branch or PR against a fixed point.\\r\\n\\r\\n   When the work goes up as a pull request, **`/pr`** shapes the body: the smallest visual that shows the change, before/after evidence that it works, and a one-way or two-way door call. It\'s model-invoked, so the agent reaches for it whenever it writes a PR.\\r\\n\\r\\n4. **`/retro`** closes the loop. After a build, and especially one that went sideways, it looks back over the session and suggests changes to the agent\'s **environment**, not the code: navigation pointers, automated checks, the coding standards `/code-review` enforces, steering files, tooling. Mechanical mistakes become deterministic checks; judgement calls become coding standards. The next build then starts from a better environment.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Context hygiene\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep steps 1–3 in **one unbroken context window** (don\'t compact or clear until after `/to-tickets`) so the grilling, spec, and tickets all build on the same thinking. Each `/implement` then starts fresh, working from the ticket. Run `/retro` in the session it\'s looking back on, before you clear; after clearing, point it at that session\'s log instead.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe limit on this is the **[smart zone](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/smart-zone)**: the window (~150k tokens on state-of-the-art models) within which the model still reasons sharply. If a session approaches it before `/to-tickets`, don\'t push on degraded; `/compact` at the nearest phase boundary and carry on (see Phase boundaries).\\r\\n\\r\\n## On-ramps\\r\\n\\r\\nA starting situation that generates work, then merges onto the main flow.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Bugs and requests piling up** → **`/triage`**. It moves issues through triage roles and produces agent-ready issues, which **`/implement`** later picks up.\\r\\n\\r\\n  Triage is only for issues **you didn\'t create**: bug reports, incoming feature requests, anything that arrives raw. Tickets that `/to-tickets` produced are already agent-ready, so **don\'t triage them**.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Something\'s broken** → **`/diagnosing-bugs`**. For the hard ones: the bug that resists a first glance, the intermittent flake, the regression that crept in between two known-good states. It refuses to theorise until it has a **tight feedback loop** (one command that already goes red on *this* bug), then fixes with a regression test. Once the fix is in, run **`/retro`** in the same session to ask what would have prevented the bug; where the real finding is that there\'s no good seam to lock it down, that\'s a job for **`/improve-codebase-architecture`**.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **A huge, foggy effort: a greenfield project or a huge feature build, too big for one session** → **`/wayfinder`**, the most cognitively demanding flow here. When the way from here to the destination isn\'t visible yet, it charts a **shared map** of **decision tickets** on the issue tracker and resolves them one at a time, producing **decisions, not deliverables**, until the fog is pushed back and the way is clear. Where **`/grill-with-docs`** sharpens an idea you can hold in one session, wayfinder is for the idea you can\'t, and it\'s slower and denser, so save it for exactly that, never a well-scoped feature.\\r\\n\\r\\n  When the map clears, **it hands off, it doesn\'t build**: merge onto the main flow at **`/to-spec`**, which collapses the map\'s linked decisions into a buildable plan, then `/to-tickets` and `/implement` as usual. Looping the map straight into `/implement` skips that collapse and throws the linked detail away, so go straight to `/implement` only when the effort turned out genuinely small.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Codebase health\\r\\n\\r\\nNot feature work, just upkeep.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **`/improve-codebase-architecture`** runs whenever you have a spare moment to keep the codebase good for agents to operate in. It surfaces **deepening opportunities**; picking one _generates an idea_ you can take into the main flow at `/grill-with-docs`. It\'s the survey that finds the candidates; **`/codebase-design`** (below) is the bench you design the chosen one on.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Vocabulary underneath\\r\\n\\r\\nTwo model-invoked references that run *beneath* the other skills, each the single source of truth for its vocabulary. Reach for them directly when the **words**, not the process, are the problem; or let the skills above pull them in.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **`/domain-modeling`**: sharpen the project\'s *domain* language: challenge a fuzzy term, resolve an overloaded word (\\"account\\" doing three jobs), record a hard-to-reverse decision as an ADR. It\'s the active discipline `/grill-with-docs` drives to keep `GLOSSARY.md` a clean glossary.\\r\\n- **`/codebase-design`** is the deep-module vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) for designing a module\'s *shape*: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface at a clean seam. `/tdd` and `/improve-codebase-architecture` both speak it.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase boundaries\\r\\n\\r\\nA **phase** is a chunk of work inside a session: the grilling, the implementation, the QA. At the **boundary** between two of them you have five options, and picking between them is the fuzziest decision in this whole map:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Continue**: stay put. Costs nothing, loses nothing.\\r\\n- **`/clear`**: empty the window, when nothing here matters to what\'s next.\\r\\n- **`/handoff`** writes a portable markdown file. Narrow: only for a **new harness**, a **new directory**, a **colleague**, or forking a side task **mid-phase**. What it buys is portability.\\r\\n- **Subagent**: send a tightly-scoped task to its own window and get a report back.\\r\\n- **`/compact`** compresses this context and seeds a fresh session with it. The **default**, at the bottom of the tree rather than the first reach.\\r\\n\\r\\nRead [PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md](PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md) for the ordered tree: the five questions, the reasoning behind each branch, and why the primary-source cost makes **Continue** the one to rule out first. Make the decision **at** a boundary; mid-phase, continue or split the rest into subagents.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Standalone\\r\\n\\r\\nOff the main flow entirely.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **`/grill-me`**: the same relentless interview as `/grill-with-docs`, but **stateless**: it saves nothing locally and builds no `GLOSSARY.md`. Reach for it when you are **not working in a working directory** (sharpening a plan, a design, a piece of writing, anything with no repo under it). If you are in a working directory, use `/grill-with-docs` instead: it runs the same interview and leaves a paper trail, so it is strictly the better one.\\r\\n- **`/grilling`** is the interview primitive itself: rounds, the frontier, facts are the agent\'s job and decisions are yours. `/grill-me` and `/grill-with-docs` are the two named ways in, and `/triage`, `/wayfinder` and `/improve-codebase-architecture` all run it internally. Reach for it directly only when you want the interview with no wrapper around it.\\r\\n- **`/prototype`** is a small, throwaway program that answers one design question: does this state model feel right, or what should this UI look like. Throwaway is a constraint on how the code is written, not a promise to destroy it: the answer folds into the real code, and the prototype itself is kept as a **primary source** on a `prototype/<name>` branch out of main, pointed at from the implementation issue. It\'s the detour in step 2 of the main flow, but reach for it any time a design question is hard to settle on paper.\\r\\n- **`/research`**: delegate reading legwork to a **background agent**: it investigates a question against **primary sources**, then leaves a cited Markdown file in the repo. Keep working while it reads. The file it produces is something to take *into* the main flow at `/grill-with-docs`, since research feeds the thinking rather than replacing it.\\r\\n- **`/to-questionnaire`** comes in when the thing blocking you isn\'t in your head or the codebase but in **someone else\'s**, and it writes them a questionnaire to fill in. It\'s the inverse of `/grill-me`: instead of interviewing you about the subject, it interviews you about the **send** (who it\'s going to, what you need back) and aims the questions at the gap. What comes back is material for `/grill-with-docs` or `/to-spec`.\\r\\n- **`/wizard`** is for the steps only a **human** can take: provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, clicking through an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, running a one-off migration or cutover. It generates an interactive bash script that opens each URL, captures each value, and writes it into `.env` and GitHub secrets, so the procedure stops being something you re-explain to an agent every time. Model-invoked, so the agent reaches for it the moment it hits a wall only you can pass. If the agent could just do it itself, it should; this is for where a human is genuinely in the loop.\\r\\n- **`/wait-what`** is the corrective for a message that didn\'t land. Use it mid-conversation, inside any other skill, and the agent re-pitches what it just said with the context you were missing, in plain English, using the `GLOSSARY.md` vocabulary. It works after the fact; `/grill-with-docs` is the upfront cure, because a shared language agreed early is what stops the jargon arriving at all.\\r\\n- **`/teach`**: learn a concept over multiple sessions, using the current directory as a stateful workspace.\\r\\n- **`/writing-for-agents`** is the reference for writing documents agents consume: skills, AGENTS.md, pointed-at docs.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Precondition\\r\\n\\r\\n**`/setup-matt-pocock-skills`**: run before your first engineering flow to configure the issue tracker, triage labels, and doc layout the other skills assume. Custom issue trackers also work.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n### skills\\\\claude\\\\canvas-design\\\\SKILL.md\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: canvas-design\\r\\ndescription: Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents using design philosophy. You should use this skill when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece. Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists\' work to avoid copyright violations.\\r\\nlicense: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nThese are instructions for creating design philosophies - aesthetic movements that are then EXPRESSED VISUALLY. Output only .md files, .pdf files, and .png files.\\r\\n\\r\\nComplete this in two steps:\\r\\n1. Design Philosophy Creation (.md file)\\r\\n2. Express by creating it on a canvas (.pdf file or .png file)\\r\\n\\r\\nFirst, undertake this task:\\r\\n\\r\\n## DESIGN PHILOSOPHY CREATION\\r\\n\\r\\nTo begin, create a VISUAL PHILOSOPHY (not layouts or templates) that will be interpreted through:\\r\\n- Form, space, color, composition\\r\\n- Images, graphics, shapes, patterns\\r\\n- Minimal text as visual accent\\r\\n\\r\\n### THE CRITICAL UNDERSTANDING\\r\\n- What is received: Some subtle input or instructions by the user that should be taken into account, but used as a foundation; it should not constrain creative freedom.\\r\\n- What is created: A design philosophy/aesthetic movement.\\r\\n- What happens next: Then, the same version receives the philosophy and EXPRESSES IT VISUALLY - creating artifacts that are 90% visual design, 10% essential text.\\r\\n\\r\\nConsider this approach:\\r\\n- Write a manifesto for an art movement\\r\\n- The next phase involves making the artwork\\r\\n\\r\\nThe philosophy must emphasize: Visual expression. Spatial communication. Artistic interpretation. Minimal words.\\r\\n\\r\\n### HOW TO GENERATE A VISUAL PHILOSOPHY\\r\\n\\r\\n**Name the movement** (1-2 words): \\"Brutalist Joy\\" / \\"Chromatic Silence\\" / \\"Metabolist Dreams\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**Articulate the philosophy** (4-6 paragraphs - concise but complete):\\r\\n\\r\\nTo capture the VISUAL essence, express how the philosophy manifests through:\\r\\n- Space and form\\r\\n- Color and material\\r\\n- Scale and rhythm\\r\\n- Composition and balance\\r\\n- Visual hierarchy\\r\\n\\r\\n**CRITICAL GUIDELINES:**\\r\\n- **Avoid redundancy**: Each design aspect should be mentioned once. Avoid repeating points about color theory, spatial relationships, or typographic principles unless adding new depth.\\r\\n- **Emphasize craftsmanship REPEATEDLY**: The philosophy MUST stress multiple times that the final work should appear as though it took countless hours to create, was labored over with care, and comes from someone at the absolute top of their field. This framing is essential - repeat phrases like \\"meticulously crafted,\\" \\"the product of deep expertise,\\" \\"painstaking attention,\\" \\"master-level execution.\\"\\r\\n- **Leave creative space**: Remain specific about the aesthetic direction, but concise enough that the next Claude has room to make interpretive choices also at a extremely high level of craftmanship.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe philosophy must guide the next version to express ideas VISUALLY, not through text. Information lives in design, not paragraphs.\\r\\n\\r\\n### PHILOSOPHY EXAMPLES\\r\\n\\r\\n**\\"Concrete Poetry\\"**\\r\\nPhilosophy: Communication through monumental form and bold geometry.\\r\\nVisual expression: Massive color blocks, sculptural typography (huge single words, tiny labels), Brutalist spatial divisions, Polish poster energy meets Le Corbusier. Ideas expressed through visual weight and spatial tension, not explanation. Text as rare, powerful gesture - never paragraphs, only essential words integrated into the visual architecture. Every element placed with the precision of a master craftsman.\\r\\n\\r\\n**\\"Chromatic Language\\"**\\r\\nPhilosophy: Color as the primary information system.\\r\\nVisual expression: Geometric precision where color zones create meaning. Typography minimal - small sans-serif labels letting chromatic fields communicate. Think Josef Albers\' interaction meets data visualization. Information encoded spatially and chromatically. Words only to anchor what color already shows. The result of painstaking chromatic calibration.\\r\\n\\r\\n**\\"Analog Meditation\\"**\\r\\nPhilosophy: Quiet visual contemplation through texture and breathing room.\\r\\nVisual expression: Paper grain, ink bleeds, vast negative space. Photography and illustration dominate. Typography whispered (small, restrained, serving the visual). Japanese photobook aesthetic. Images breathe across pages. Text appears sparingly - short phrases, never explanatory blocks. Each composition balanced with the care of a meditation practice.\\r\\n\\r\\n**\\"Organic Systems\\"**\\r\\nPhilosophy: Natural clustering and modular growth patterns.\\r\\nVisual expression: Rounded forms, organic arrangements, color from nature through architecture. Information shown through visual diagrams, spatial relationships, iconography. Text only for key labels floating in space. The composition tells the story through expert spatial orchestration.\\r\\n\\r\\n**\\"Geometric Silence\\"**\\r\\nPhilosophy: Pure order and restraint.\\r\\nVisual expression: Grid-based precision, bold photography or stark graphics, dramatic negative space. Typography precise but minimal - small essential text, large quiet zones. Swiss formalism meets Brutalist material honesty. Structure communicates, not words. Every alignment the work of countless refinements.\\r\\n\\r\\n*These are condensed examples. The actual design philosophy should be 4-6 substantial paragraphs.*\\r\\n\\r\\n### ESSENTIAL PRINCIPLES\\r\\n- **VISUAL PHILOSOPHY**: Create an aesthetic worldview to be expressed through design\\r\\n- **MINIMAL TEXT**: Always emphasize that text is sparse, essential-only, integrated as visual element - never lengthy\\r\\n- **SPATIAL EXPRESSION**: Ideas communicate through space, form, color, composition - not paragraphs\\r\\n- **ARTISTIC FREEDOM**: The next Claude interprets the philosophy visually - provide creative room\\r\\n- **PURE DESIGN**: This is about making ART OBJECTS, not documents with decoration\\r\\n- **EXPERT CRAFTSMANSHIP**: Repeatedly emphasize the final work must look meticulously crafted, labored over with care, the product of countless hours by someone at the top of their field\\r\\n\\r\\n**The design philosophy should be 4-6 paragraphs long.** Fill it with poetic design philosophy that brings together the core vision. Avoid repeating the same points. Keep the design philosophy generic without mentioning the intention of the art, as if it can be used wherever. Output the design philosophy as a .md file.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## DEDUCING THE SUBTLE REFERENCE\\r\\n\\r\\n**CRITICAL STEP**: Before creating the canvas, identify the subtle conceptual thread from the original request.\\r\\n\\r\\n**THE ESSENTIAL PRINCIPLE**:\\r\\nThe topic is a **subtle, niche reference embedded within the art itself** - not always literal, always sophisticated. Someone familiar with the subject should feel it intuitively, while others simply experience a masterful abstract composition. The design philosophy provides the aesthetic language. The deduced topic provides the soul - the quiet conceptual DNA woven invisibly into form, color, and composition.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is **VERY IMPORTANT**: The reference must be refined so it enhances the work\'s depth without announcing itself. Think like a jazz musician quoting another song - only those who know will catch it, but everyone appreciates the music.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## CANVAS CREATION\\r\\n\\r\\nWith both the philosophy and the conceptual framework established, express it on a canvas. Take a moment to gather thoughts and clear the mind. Use the design philosophy created and the instructions below to craft a masterpiece, embodying all aspects of the philosophy with expert craftsmanship.\\r\\n\\r\\n**IMPORTANT**: For any type of content, even if the user requests something for a movie/game/book, the approach should still be sophisticated. Never lose sight of the idea that this should be art, not something that\'s cartoony or amateur.\\r\\n\\r\\nTo create museum or magazine quality work, use the design philosophy as the foundation. Create one single page, highly visual, design-forward PDF or PNG output (unless asked for more pages). Generally use repeating patterns and perfect shapes. Treat the abstract philosophical design as if it were a scientific bible, borrowing the visual language of systematic observation—dense accumulation of marks, repeated elements, or layered patterns that build meaning through patient repetition and reward sustained viewing. Add sparse, clinical typography and systematic reference markers that suggest this could be a diagram from an imaginary discipline, treating the invisible subject with the same reverence typically reserved for documenting observable phenomena. Anchor the piece with simple phrase(s) or details positioned subtly, using a limited color palette that feels intentional and cohesive. Embrace the paradox of using analytical visual language to express ideas about human experience: the result should feel like an artifact that proves something ephemeral can be studied, mapped, and understood through careful attention. This is true art. \\r\\n\\r\\n**Text as a contextual element**: Text is always minimal and visual-first, but let context guide whether that means whisper-quiet labels or bold typographic gestures. A punk venue poster might have larger, more aggressive type than a minimalist ceramics studio identity. Most of the time, font should be thin. All use of fonts must be design-forward and prioritize visual communication. Regardless of text scale, nothing falls off the page and nothing overlaps. Every element must be contained within the canvas boundaries with proper margins. Check carefully that all text, graphics, and visual elements have breathing room and clear separation. This is non-negotiable for professional execution. **IMPORTANT: Use different fonts if writing text. Search the `./canvas-fonts` directory. Regardless of approach, sophistication is non-negotiable.**\\r\\n\\r\\nDownload and use whatever fonts are needed to make this a reality. Get creative by making the typography actually part of the art itself -- if the art is abstract, bring the font onto the canvas, not typeset digitally.\\r\\n\\r\\nTo push boundaries, follow design instinct/intuition while using the philosophy as a guiding principle. Embrace ultimate design freedom and choice. Push aesthetics and design to the frontier. \\r\\n\\r\\n**CRITICAL**: To achieve human-crafted quality (not AI-generated), create work that looks like it took countless hours. Make it appear as though someone at the absolute top of their field labored over every detail with painstaking care. Ensure the composition, spacing, color choices, typography - everything screams expert-level craftsmanship. Double-check that nothing overlaps, formatting is flawless, every detail perfect. Create something that could be shown to people to prove expertise and rank as undeniably impressive.\\r\\n\\r\\nOutput the final result as a single, downloadable .pdf or .png file, alongside the design philosophy used as a .md file.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## FINAL STEP\\r\\n\\r\\n**IMPORTANT**: The user ALREADY said \\"It isn\'t perfect enough. It must be pristine, a masterpiece if craftsmanship, as if it were about to be displayed in a museum.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**CRITICAL**: To refine the work, avoid adding more graphics; instead refine what has been created and make it extremely crisp, respecting the design philosophy and the principles of minimalism entirely. Rather than adding a fun filter or refactoring a font, consider how to make the existing composition more cohesive with the art. If the instinct is to call a new function or draw a new shape, STOP and instead ask: \\"How can I make what\'s already here more of a piece of art?\\"\\r\\n\\r\\nTake a second pass. Go back to the code and refine/polish further to make this a philosophically designed masterpiece.\\r\\n\\r\\n## MULTI-PAGE OPTION\\r\\n\\r\\nTo create additional pages when requested, create more creative pages along the same lines as the design philosophy but distinctly different as well. Bundle those pages in the same .pdf or many .pngs. Treat the first page as just a single page in a whole coffee table book waiting to be filled. Make the next pages unique twists and memories of the original. Have them almost tell a story in a very tasteful way. Exercise full creative freedom.\\r\\n\\r\\n### skills\\\\claude\\\\chat-export\\\\SKILL.md\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: chat-export\\r\\ndescription: Save the current conversation as a structured markdown file and generate a handoff prompt for continuing in a new chat. Use this skill whenever the user says \\"export this chat\\", \\"save this conversation\\", \\"create a handoff\\", \\"save this for later\\", \\"export to my chat exports folder\\", or anything indicating they want to preserve a conversation and carry context into a new session. Always trigger this skill proactively when a conversation has been long, complex, or has produced decisions, files, or code — even if the user hasn\'t explicitly asked yet.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Chat Export Skill\\r\\n\\r\\nSaves the current conversation as a structured markdown file to\\r\\n`C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/handoffs/` with a full transcript,\\r\\nsummary, and a paste-ready handoff prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output path\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nC:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/handoffs/YYYY-MM-DD_short-title.md\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse today\'s date. Make the short title 3-5 words, kebab-case,\\r\\ndescribing what the chat was about.\\r\\n\\r\\nExample: `2026-04-28_claude-folder-cleanup-notebooklm.md`\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Reconstruct the full transcript** from the conversation in context.\\r\\n   Write every user message and every Claude reply verbatim under\\r\\n   `### User` and `### Claude` headings. Do not paraphrase or skip.\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **Write the structured summary** (see template below).\\r\\n\\r\\n3. **Write the handoff prompt** — a single paste-ready block the user\\r\\n   can drop into a new chat to resume instantly. It should:\\r\\n   - Point to the file: `Read C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/handoffs/<filename>.md`\\r\\n   - State what was done\\r\\n   - State what to do next (ask the user if unclear)\\r\\n\\r\\n4. **Save the file** using Desktop Commander\'s `write_file` to the\\r\\n   output path above.\\r\\n\\r\\n5. **Tell the user**:\\r\\n   - The filename\\r\\n   - The handoff prompt (show it in a code block so it\'s easy to copy)\\r\\n\\r\\n## File template\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\n# <Chat title>\\r\\n\\r\\n**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD\\r\\n**Topic:** one-line description\\r\\n**Tags:** (pick relevant: lsat-u | lsat-content | applications | tooling | drive-organizer | theology | general)\\r\\n**File:** C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/handoffs/<filename>.md\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Summary\\r\\n\\r\\nOne paragraph. What was this chat about, what was the goal, what was accomplished.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What was decided / built\\r\\n\\r\\n- bullet list of concrete outcomes, decisions, files created, commands run\\r\\n\\r\\n## Open threads\\r\\n\\r\\n- things not finished\\r\\n- questions still unresolved\\r\\n- next steps\\r\\n\\r\\n## Handoff prompt\\r\\n\\r\\n> Paste this into a new chat to continue:\\r\\n>\\r\\n> ```\\r\\n> Read C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/handoffs/<filename>.md and continue\\r\\n> from where we left off. [Specific next thing to do goes here.]\\r\\n> ```\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Full transcript\\r\\n\\r\\n### User\\r\\n[message]\\r\\n\\r\\n### Claude\\r\\n[reply]\\r\\n\\r\\n[...repeat for every message in the conversation...]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Notes\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never truncate the transcript. If it\'s long, write all of it.\\r\\n- The \\"Open threads\\" section is the most important part for handoffs —\\r\\n  be precise about what is unfinished.\\r\\n- If the user specifies a subfolder (e.g. \\"save this under lsat-u\\"),\\r\\n  save to `C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/handoffs/lsat-u/<filename>.md`\\r\\n  and create the folder if it doesn\'t exist.\\r\\n- After saving, always show the handoff prompt in a fenced code block\\r\\n  so the user can copy it in one click.\\r\\n\\r\\n"}'}]
